Regression coverage checks capability inference for provider-prefixed IDs, Vertex display names, thinking options on all five Claude routes, and actual Anthropic SDK request serialization for provider-default, disabled, and active thinking. Implementation verification recorded in the companion plan also covers live Anthropic and Bedrock requests; live Vertex verification remains untested because Google credentials were unavailable.

title: Let providers.json name a command that supplies an API key
description:
This PR adds an `apiKeyHelper` setting to provider blocks in `providers.json`, so that a user or administrator can point a provider at a command that prints its API key (useful for keys that rotate or come from a secrets vault). This is the configuration half of posit-dev/assistant#2670; the assistant app is what actually runs the command.

```jsonc
"anthropic": {
  "apiKeyHelper": {
    "command": "vault",
    "args": ["kv", "get", "-field=api_key", "secret/anthropic"],
    "timeoutMs": 10000,
    "refreshIntervalMs": 300000
  }
}
```

The config package only validates the setting and passes it through to the resolved provider list; it never runs anything. `command` is required. With `args`, the program runs directly; without `args`, `command` is a single shell line. The setting is accepted on built-in providers that authenticate with an API key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, OpenAI-compatible, Microsoft Foundry, LiteLLM, Portkey, OpenCode) and on the matching custom provider types. It's rejected on Snowflake Cortex, where the selected Snowflake connection would take precedence over a key, and on providers that don't use a key.

Edge behavior:

- An enforced `apiKeyHelper` replaces the user's whole `apiKeyHelper` instead of merging field by field, so an enforced `{ "command": ... }` never picks up a user's `args` or timeout. A custom provider or model that happens to be named `apiKeyHelper` still merges normally.
- Built-in defaults never supply a helper; it only comes from a provider block.
- Editing a helper counts as a connection change, so apps refetch that provider's models.

The JSON schema is regenerated, and the setting and its merge rule are documented in the memory bank.

title: Stop offering "Off" thinking for GPT-6.1 Sol on Bedrock
description:
When a user picks GPT-6.1 Sol through Amazon Bedrock, the thinking menu offers "Off". Choosing it sends the reasoning effort "none", which Bedrock rejects. The direct OpenAI provider already hid "Off" for this model, but Bedrock kept its own copy of the GPT-6 rules, and the two copies had drifted apart.

This PR moves the GPT-6 traits that are the same on every endpoint into one shared definition that both the OpenAI and Bedrock capability tables use. Those traits are the model family, tool and image/PDF support, and which models can't turn thinking off. As a result:

- GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, including dated IDs, offer Low, Medium, High, Xhigh, and Max on both providers.
- Original GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, and unknown future GPT-6 models still offer "Off".

Each provider keeps its own token limits and routing, so those don't change. On Bedrock, exact Astra IDs keep the published 1.05M context window and 128K output limit. Other GPT-6 models on Bedrock keep a 1M window with no assumed output limit, even when they share Astra's thinking levels. OpenAI keeps 1.05M/128K for the whole family. User-specified capability overrides still take precedence, including an override that adds "Off" back.

title: Add a Portkey key type and explain invalid providers.json saves
description:
This PR makes two independent improvements:

1. A new `keyType` setting for the built-in Portkey provider says whether the API key is a Portkey API key (`"portkey"`) or the upstream provider's key (`"upstream"`), so that Portkey works through a corporate proxy in front of hosted Portkey and through Portkey hybrid or enterprise gateways.
2. When providers.json is invalid, or a change would make it invalid, updating the file now fails with a typed error that says why, so that hosts can show the user what to fix instead of a generic failure.

Today the base URL decides what the Portkey key means: `https://api.portkey.ai` means a Portkey key, and any other URL means an upstream provider's key. A user whose company routes hosted Portkey through its own proxy has a Portkey key on a non-Portkey URL. The provider treated that key as an upstream key: it added `/v1` to the URL, sent the key in the upstream's auth header, and injected a routing header, so every request failed.

With key type `"portkey"` on any URL other than hosted Portkey, the provider now matches the request a user would send with curl:

- It uses the URL exactly as entered (a trailing `/` is trimmed). Users include `/v1` if their gateway needs it.
- It sends the key only as `x-portkey-api-key`, with no `Authorization` or `x-api-key` header.
- It injects no `x-portkey-provider` routing header.
- It accepts both bare model IDs (`claude-sonnet-4-6`) and catalog IDs (`@anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`).
- It discovers models from `<base URL>/models`. If that request fails, the existing cache and declared-models fallback applies.

When `keyType` is unset, the key type is inferred from the URL exactly as before, so existing configs behave the same. The key type can also come from the `PORTKEY_KEY_TYPE` environment variable or an administrator's config, and the resolved catalog reports where it came from so forms can show it read-only.

One shared check owns the rules that combine the base URL, key type, and key presence. The provider runs it on the effective connection before each request, and it's exported so that hosts can run it at save time. It reports a missing base URL, the `api.portkey.ai` host on anything other than exactly `https://api.portkey.ai`, key type `"upstream"` with the hosted URL, and key type `"portkey"` with no key. It takes only whether a key is present, never the key itself. These rules deliberately live outside the strict schema, so a bad combination can never make providers.json invalid and block every later save.

The invalid-file error distinguishes a file that is already invalid from a change that would make it invalid. For a syntax error it carries the line and column; for a schema error it carries each problem's path and message. Messages never include the values found in the file, so a secret in a custom header can't leak into an error shown to the user.

## Changes

- providers.json accepts `providers.portkey.keyType` (`"portkey"` or `"upstream"`), and the published JSON schema describes it.
- The resolved Portkey connection includes the key type and its source (user file, environment, or administrator), including the key type a lower layer provides when the user clears theirs.
- Runtime API-key credentials can carry the Portkey key type. The credential store never persists it; it always comes from config.
- Exported helpers return the key type a URL implies and check a whole Portkey connection.
- Updating providers.json throws a typed, secret-safe error when the file is invalid before or after the change. Previously, the caller received an untyped error with no structured detail.
- Type-mismatch schema messages name the expected type only. Previously, they could include the received value.

## Not included

- Custom `type: "portkey"` entries don't get `keyType`; they keep the URL-based behavior. That needs changes to the custom schema, forms, and discovery policy, and is a follow-up.
- Discovery at `<base URL>/models` and header-only auth through the customer's proxy haven't been confirmed against the real proxy yet. If they don't hold, the gateway mode needs rework before release.

## Breaking changes

Older clients share `~/.posit/ai/providers.json`, and their strict schema skips a `portkey` block that sets `keyType`. The monorepo's writers therefore write `keyType` only when it differs from the key type the URL implies, so hosted users keep a config older clients can read.

title: Fix no-parameter tool calls failing on OpenAI-compatible streams
description:
When a model on an OpenAI-compatible provider (Microsoft Foundry, Databricks, Snowflake, or a generic OpenAI-compatible endpoint) calls a tool that takes no parameters, the call always fails. Its arguments arrive as `{}{}` instead of `{}`, which isn't valid JSON. In Posit Assistant this means the user can never leave Plan mode, and the model retries the same failing call in a loop (posit-dev/assistant#2658).

This PR removes the response fix-up that caused it. For tools without parameters, the fix-up replaced an empty first arguments fragment with `{}`. A standard stream sends an empty fragment first and `{}` in a later chunk, and the AI SDK joins the fragments, so the call ended up as `{}` + `{}`.

Providers that send only an empty fragment for a no-parameter tool still work, because the AI SDK already treats empty tool input as `{}`. A new test covers that case.

The fix-up dates from April but did no harm until the August update of `@ai-sdk/openai` from 3.0.71 to 3.0.88. Before that update, the SDK treated a tool call as finished as soon as its arguments parsed as JSON and ignored the later `{}`.

Needed for posit-dev/assistant#2660.

## Design decisions

- **Delete instead of making the fix-up remember earlier chunks.** A version that injects `{}` only when no arguments arrived would have to keep per-stream state and add synthetic events at the end of the stream. Nothing downstream needs it anymore: the SDK no longer parses arguments mid-stream, and both the SDK and Posit Assistant map empty input to `{}`.
- **Numbering kept.** The remaining response fix-ups keep their numbers (5 is marked retired), because documentation refers to them by number.

## Verification

The new wire test streams fake server events through the real middleware, `@ai-sdk/openai`, and `streamText`. On the old code, the empty-then-`{}` case fails with the customer's exact error (`JSON parsing failed: Text: {}{}`). Because the test drives the real SDK, a future SDK update that changes how tool arguments are joined will also fail it.

title: Add Posit Connect device sign-in to ai-credentials
description:
## Summary

Adds Posit Connect's OAuth device-code sign-in to `ai-credentials`, so every store-backed host (Positron, standalone, RStudio, TUI) shares one implementation.

- **The server URL is stored with the credential.** An `oauth-device` source can now carry an optional `serverUrl`, like Databricks' workspace host. The host writes it with a `replace` mutation before sign-in, and `StoreBackend` keeps it in `oauthAuth.serverUrl` through every later record (pending, authenticated, refreshed, terminal). It's reported as status `metadata.serverUrl` and passed to `oauthConfigForProvider` on the stored source context (`CredentialSourceContext` gains the same optional field).
- **The token can't be sent to a different server.** The host resolves the grant from the stored URL, and the grant's `credentialBaseUrl` is that same URL. So the shaped `{ type: "apikey", apiKey, baseUrl }` credential, and every refresh, target the server that issued the token. Configuring a different server replaces the record and drops the old token.
- **`connect-oauth.ts`.** `createConnectDeviceCodeGrantResolver()` does RFC 8414 discovery and RFC 7591 client registration. Setup is bounded by a 30s deadline and memoized per normalized server, and failures are evicted so a later attempt retries. `normalizeConnectBaseUrl` is the shared URL policy: https or loopback http, no userinfo, query, or fragment.
- **No `CONNECT_API_KEY` env mapping.** Connect credentials come only from sign-in or a host-managed source such as Workbench. The `POSIT_CONNECT_URL` connection mapping in ai-config is unchanged.
- Updates `memory-bank/credentialResolver.md`.

Hosts that pin a server (`POSIT_CONNECT_URL` or a `providers.json` URL) enforce that themselves by resolving no grant for a stored server that doesn't match. ai-lib needs no knowledge of pinning.

## Testing

- `npm run check-types` and `npm run format:check` pass.
- `connect-oauth.test.ts` covers discovery, issuer paths, memoization, the setup timeout and retry, issuer mismatch, cross-origin endpoints, non-loopback http, and IPv6 loopback.
- `StoreBackend.test.ts` covers the stored server reaching the grant, status metadata, and the shaped credential, and that configuring a different server drops the old token.
- One existing failure, unrelated to this change: the `SingleFileStore` cross-process lock test. On Node 26 the child process prints a `module.register()` deprecation warning, and the test expects empty stderr.

Consumed by the Posit Assistant branch `worktree-positron-connect-device-signin`.

title: Report the Posit AI Pass account email while setup is pending
description:
This PR makes two changes to how the Posit AI Pass provider fetches its model list:

1. While the account's setup is pending, the provider looks up the signed-in account's email and reports it alongside the pending status, so that host apps can add it to posit.ai's setup link (`/setup?email=...`) and posit.ai can show "Wrong Account" when the browser is signed in as someone else.
2. The provider's cached model list and status now belong to the exact access token that produced them, so that after an account switch or sign-out the app never shows the previous account's models or status.

The email closes a gap in setup: when a user signs in to Posit Assistant as one account while their browser is signed in to posit.ai as another, "Complete setup" finishes setup for the browser's account, and the Assistant's account stays pending. posit.ai now accepts an expected email on its pages (posit-hosted/prism-ui#315); this PR supplies it.

The lookup is off unless the host app supplies a list of candidate login hosts; the Posit Assistant wiring comes in a separate PR. The provider sends the access token only to a host that provably issued it. It checks the token's signature against each candidate host's published public keys and uses the first host whose keys match. It then asks that host for the current user, and accepts the email only if the returned user ID matches the token's.

If anything goes wrong, the provider reports pending status without an email, and the setup link works as it does today. That covers no candidate hosts, an `http://` or malformed host, a signature that no host's keys verify, a failed key or user lookup, a redirect to the login page, and a lookup that takes longer than 5 seconds. Failed lookups retry on the next model-list refresh; a successful lookup is reused for the same token and hosts, even across cache clears. The token, the email, and the user response are never logged.

A model-list response that finishes after a sign-out, token change, or cache clear is now discarded instead of overwriting newer state. The cost is one extra model-list request each time the access token refreshes.

Part of posit-dev/assistant#2560. Related to posit-hosted/prism-ui#293

## Changes

- Provider registration accepts an optional getter of candidate login hosts (`getPositAiAuthHostCandidates` on the registration config, or a fifth argument to `registerPositAiProvider`). Hosts can be bare (`login.posit.cloud`) or `https://` URLs. Without it, behavior is unchanged apart from the token-keyed cache.
- The pending status can carry `accountEmail`. It appears only with `agreement_pending`, and only when the lookup succeeded.
- A new or missing access token clears the cached model list and status. Previously, the cache was served regardless of which token filled it, and signing out cleared only the status.

## Design decisions

- **Signature check instead of the issuer claim.** The token's issuer claim is `lucid:services:lucid-auth`, which names no host. Staging and production publish the same key ID with different keys, so verifying the signature is what tells them apart. It also works for tokens stored before an auth-host edit, without persisting anything new.
- **Ordered candidates instead of one host.** Positron's sign-in and Posit Assistant's configuration can disagree about the login host on older Positron versions. Using the first candidate that verifies the token covers both without version checks.
- **Keyed on the full token, not the user ID.** The user ID claim can't be trusted before the signature check, and user IDs can repeat across environments, so a claim-based key could hand one account's email to another.

## Not included

- Supplying the candidate hosts from Posit Assistant (Node and Positron), and showing the email in the setup banner and configuration overlay. Those land in the Posit Assistant repo.

title: Add GPT-6.1 Sol to direct OpenAI model lists
description:
This PR adds GPT-6.1 Sol to direct OpenAI model lists, so users can select it by name whether OpenAI's live model list loads or the app falls back to its built-in list.

The model offers five reasoning levels: low, medium, high, extra high, and max. OpenAI does not accept "off" for this model, so the app no longer offers it. GPT-6.1 Sol shares the existing GPT-6 Astra reasoning rule and its documented context and output limits.

Other providers that use the same OpenAI reasoning rules also stop offering "off" for GPT-6.1 Sol, but this PR does not add the model to those providers' lists.

title: Record the source of local provider endpoints
description:
The catalog now reports where the Ollama and LM Studio endpoint came from (user, enforced, environment, or default), the same way it already does for Foundry and OpenCode fields.

Posit Assistant stores its own local endpoint outside `providers.json`, and needs to know whether the catalog's endpoint was enforced or set in the environment, since only those override the stored one. Comparing the value against the built-in endpoint gets this wrong when an admin enforces `http://localhost:11434`: the enforced value looks like the default, so a user's saved endpoint replaces it.

Also adds the custom-provider registration tests that posit-dev/assistant#2578 removes from Assistant's Node tests. Their assertions are identical; they now call ai-lib's `registerAllProviders` directly:
- each supported custom kind dispatches to its own registrar
- custom `aws`, `google-vertex`, `snowflake` and `ms-foundry` entries receive their callbacks and credential environment

Addresses feedback from https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/2578#pullrequestreview-5361592059

> - **important (correctness)** — `packages/node/src/platform/services/catalogCredentials.ts:262-265, 359-361`: the new rule for local endpoints lets a saved user endpoint override an admin-enforced or environment endpoint when that value happens to equal a built-in default.
> 
>   `isBuiltInLocalEndpoint` decides that the catalog's endpoint "carries no user or admin intent" by comparing it with `OLLAMA_DEFAULTS.endpoint` / `LMSTUDIO_DEFAULTS.endpoint`. It doesn't check where the value came from.
> 
>   Example: an admin enforces `ollama.endpoint = "http://localhost:11434"` to keep Ollama traffic on the machine. A user who previously saved `http://gpu-box:11434` still gets `gpu-box`, because the enforced value looks like the default.
> 
>   This also contradicts the documented policy, which this PR doesn't update:
>   - the function's own doc comment (lines 218-223: "Catalog values win for connection fields because the resolved catalog has already applied user/admin/default precedence")
>   - `memory-bank/providerBridge.md:93`
>   - `memory-bank/positronIntegration.md:754`
> 
>   The change applies to Positron too, through `credential-monitor.ts:271`.
> 
>   Suggested fix: ai-config already records a per-field source (`user | enforced | environment | default`) for ms-foundry `baseUrl` and the opencode fields (`fieldSourceFor` in `resolve-catalog.ts`). Record an `endpoint` source for local providers the same way. Then let the stored endpoint win only when that source is `"default"`. If the value check stays as a stopgap, update the doc comment and the two memory-bank lines, and name the limitation.
>

title: Provider credential fixes and shared custom-provider registration
description:
This PR fills some gaps in the ai-lib's authentication process to bring it to parity with Positron's Authentication extension and adds shared custom-provider registration for Positron's headless service. 

This carries the ai-lib changes from #114 that don't depend on the auth id rename.

- Two windows refreshing the same OAuth credential no longer overwrite each other's tokens. A refresh commits only while the stored record still holds the generation it read. The device-code poll also logs the error code an attempt ends with.
- If `GEMINI_API_KEY` is unset, the Gemini provider reads `GOOGLE_API_KEY`.
- Google Vertex accepts a service account from `GOOGLE_CLIENT_EMAIL` and `GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY`, and tries it before Application Default Credentials. If Google rejects the credentials, the provider reports an auth error that names the two variables.
- On Posit Workbench, an admin-provisioned Databricks profile takes precedence over a `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` in the user's shell.
- The bridge registers `providers.custom` entries by kind, with shared helpers for a custom entry's auth mapping and for writing Google Cloud and AWS session tokens, for Positron's headless language model service and Assistant to share.
- When `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` is set, the AWS credential provider points the STS token exchange at the configured region.
- The catalog loader accepts defaults from the host, and ai-config can normalize a Microsoft Foundry base URL, both for Assistant's upcoming provider path.

Cherry-picked from #114. Where they conflicted, I kept main's OpenCode entries and #119's "Reload model list" wording.

title: Cap DeepSeek V4 Flash max output at 262,144 on Posit AI Pass
description:
Using DeepSeek V4 Flash through Posit AI Pass fails with:

```
Error making request (HTTP 400): Invalid request: ['max_tokens (384000): Input should be less than or equal to 262144']
```

The Model APIs capability entry for `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` used `maxOutputTokens: 384_000`, which is DeepSeek's native API limit. Baseten Model APIs caps this model at 262,144, so this lowers the entry to `262_144` and adds a comment explaining the discrepancy.

The direct DeepSeek provider entries in `deepseek-helpers.ts` are unchanged, since they target DeepSeek's own API where 384K is the documented limit.

ai-config model-capabilities tests pass.

title: Fix GPT OSS tool calls on Databricks
description:
Fix GPT OSS tool calls on Databricks.

## Problem

GPT OSS models on Databricks lose their tool call arguments. The tool then runs with `{}` and fails schema checks. There are two causes:

1. On chat completions, Databricks sends `delta.content` as an array of reasoning parts. The OpenAI spec says it must be a string or null. The AI SDK rejects the whole chunk, and the tool arguments are in that same chunk.
2. On the AI Gateway, we route GPT OSS to the unified Responses API. That route streams GPT OSS tool calls with `arguments: ""` in every event. Qwen and Llama stream their arguments correctly.

## Changes

- `openai-compat-fetch.ts`: new transform 7. It turns array `content` into its text parts, or `null`, and drops reasoning parts. The SDK already rejected array content for all providers, so this cannot break a provider that works today.
- `databricks-helpers.ts`: `gpt-oss*` models do not get the `mlflow-responses` protocol. They use `openai-chat`, which they also advertise.
- `memory-bank/aiConfig.md`: records the behaviour and the date we observed it.

## Known limits

- Reasoning text is still dropped on chat completions.
- Chat completions can also drop GPT OSS output completely on large requests with many tools. That is a Databricks issue, and we are reporting it to them.

## Testing

- New tests: captured Databricks chunks through the middleware and `streamText`, and the GPT OSS routing rule. Both fail without the fix.
- Checked by hand in Positron with `databricks-gpt-oss-120b` through the AI Gateway.

title: Add Claude Sonnet 5.5 model support
description:
This PR adds Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, released 2026-09-28) to the model catalog, so it shows up with the right context limits and thinking-effort options on Anthropic, Posit AI Pass, Bedrock, and OpenRouter-style IDs.

- **Capability rule** (`ai-config`): 1M context, 128K max output, family `claude-5.5`. It sits before the broader `^claude-sonnet-5` rule, which would otherwise match it.
- **No "off" thinking level.** Sonnet 5.5 thinks adaptively by default, and `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` returns a 400. Our "off" works by leaving the `thinking` field out, which on this model would still think, at the API's default effort, with thinking text omitted. So "off" isn't offered, same as for Opus 5.5. The model's real lowest setting, `thinking: {type: "between_tools"}`, isn't wired into the clients.
- **Supplemental Anthropic model entry**, so Sonnet 5.5 appears in the selector until `/v1/models` returns it.
- **No Posit AI Pass supersession of Sonnet 5.** Sonnet 5.5 has breaking API changes, so Sonnet 5 stays selectable. The picker moves it to the "More models" submenu.

Companion monorepo PR: pins the submodule to this change and adds pricing and model-picker defaults.

## Verification

- New tests cover the Sonnet 5.5 rule for bare, Bedrock-prefixed, and dot-separated IDs, and confirm plain `claude-sonnet-5` still gets the Sonnet 5 rule with "off".
- `ai-config` model-capability tests, `ai-provider-bridge` provider tests, and type checks pass.

title: Use catalog ids as auth provider ids
description:
Renames every `PROVIDER_MAP` auth provider id to match its catalog id, so `authProviderId` equals the catalog id for every provider except `copilot` and `posit-connect`, which keep the ids their integration partners own. Positron's auth extension and Assistant both read `PROVIDER_MAP`, and this is the first of three coordinated PRs (this one, then Positron, then Assistant) that move authentication ownership for seven providers to Assistant.

- Renames `PROVIDER_MAP`'s `authProviderId` values to the catalog ids (`anthropic`, `openai`, `gemini`, `deepseek`, `bedrock`, `google-vertex`, `positai`) and re-keys `CONFIG_KEY_OVERRIDES` so every provider's legacy `authentication.*` settings section stays the same.
- Adds `POSITRON_LEGACY_AUTH_PROVIDER_IDS`, mapping each catalog id to the auth id Positron registered before the rename, so Assistant can detect an older Positron and Positron core can copy credentials stored under the old ids.
- Keeps the retired vendor strings (`anthropic-api`, `posit-ai`, `openai-api`, `google`, `deepseek-api`, `google-cloud`) resolving to their catalog ids in `vscode.lm` vendor lookup, so an already-registered model still maps correctly.
- Adds `GOOGLE_API_KEY` as a fallback for the Gemini env credential, behind `GEMINI_API_KEY`, matching how Positron's own extension resolves the key today.
- Adds a `hostDefaults` layer to the catalog loader (both load and watch paths), ranked below the user's `providers.json` and after `POSIT_AI_PROVIDERS_DEFAULT`, so a host can set a default like the Positron `positaiLogin.clientId` (`positron`, instead of the general default `rstudio-ide`) without it overriding what a user has actually set.

## Phase 2

- Added `normalizeFoundryBaseUrl` to ai-config, normalizing a pasted Microsoft Foundry endpoint to its `/openai/v1` base URL.
- Google Vertex now resolves access tokens from inline service-account environment variables (`GOOGLE_CLIENT_EMAIL`/`GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY`/`GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY_ID`) before falling back to Application Default Credentials.
- `registerAllProviders` can register `providers.custom` entries directly, so a host with no built-in provider list can still serve a custom gateway, Bedrock-shaped, Snowflake-shaped, or Google Vertex-shaped credential. Added a shared `customProviderAuthMapping` rule and a `serializeSessionToken`/`shapeCredentials` round trip so hosts stop hand-rolling custom-entry auth mappings and session-token envelopes.
- A Workbench-managed Databricks profile now suppresses `DATABRICKS_TOKEN` from the environment resolver, so an admin-provisioned credential can't be shadowed from a shell.
- Reserved `github`, `posit-connect-llm`, `custom-providers`, and `positron-custom-provider` as custom-provider names, since they'd otherwise collide with another product's auth-provider id.

title: Export the per-provider catalog diff from ai-config/node
description:
This PR adds `diffProviderCatalogs(previous, current)` to `ai-config/node`. For each provider that differs between two catalogs, it reports whether the provider was added, removed, or updated, and for updates, whether its enabled state, connection, or models changed. The catalog watcher now computes its aggregate change flags from this function, so hosts that install catalogs themselves use the same classification as the watcher. Watcher behavior is unchanged.

The assistant monorepo already depends on this export: https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/2531 (merged) calls it from `ProviderCatalogService`, and it pinned the submodule to this change on the unmerged `export-catalog-diff` branch. Once another monorepo PR moved the pin to ai-lib main, the build broke because main doesn't export the function. Merging this PR puts the function on main.

This is the `export-catalog-diff` commit cherry-picked onto the current main (after #119), with no conflicts. https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/2559 will pin the merged commit.

title: Rename Refresh Models notification action to Reload model list
description:
This PR renames the "Refresh Models" action on the AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex credential notifications to "Reload model list", and updates the instructions in those messages to match, so that they use the same name as Posit Assistant's model menu. For example, the expired-SSO message now ends "...to refresh your session, then click Reload model list."

"Refresh Models" read as if it updated or reset the models themselves; the action actually clears the cached model list and asks each provider for its current models, so the new name describes the list.

Only the displayed text changes. The action's identifier is unchanged, so hosts that show the label from the notification pick up the new text without code changes.


This goes along with https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/2559.

title: Send a host User-Agent on Posit Connect gateway requests
description:
Posit Connect gateway requests don't currently say which host sent them. This PR lets hosts pass a `connectUserAgent` at provider registration, and that value is sent on Connect model discovery and chat requests.

- If the credentials already set a User-Agent header (matched case-insensitively), that configured value wins.
- The change lives in `providers/connect-provider.ts`, plus a small `withDefaultUserAgent` helper in `custom-headers.ts`.

## Testing

New tests in `connect-provider.test.ts` check that the host User-Agent is sent on both discovery requests and on Anthropic and Bedrock gateway chats, where it sits alongside configured custom headers. They also check that a configured User-Agent header overrides it.

## Commits

- [6b138d3](https://github.com/posit-dev/ai-lib/commit/6b138d3) - Send a host User-Agent on Posit Connect gateway requests

title: Add Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 model support
description:
This PR adds Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6 family (Astra, Sol, Luna) to the model catalogs in ai-config and ai-provider-bridge, so clients can list the new models with correct context limits, output caps, and thinking-effort levels.

ai-config gains capability rules: Opus 5.5 with a 1M context, 128K output, and always-on adaptive thinking (no "off" level); GPT-6 with a 1.05M context, 128K output, and xhigh/max effort levels, with Astra omitting the off level. Bedrock Mantle gets a matching Astra rule (GA since 2026-09-08, documented 1.05M/128K).

In the bridge, the OpenAI provider gains display names for the three models, its live model-list filter now keeps gpt-6 IDs (previously only gpt-5/gpt-4/o prefixes were kept, so GPT-6 IDs would have been dropped), and static fallback rows list the family when the endpoint is unreachable. Anthropic gets a supplemental Opus 5.5 entry that is de-duped against the live model list until the endpoint returns it. Posit AI Pass gains a supersession from Claude Opus 5 to Opus 5.5, inert until the gateway serves 5.5.

Edge and fallback behavior: unknown future gpt-6 IDs default to the 1.05M context window (1M via Bedrock), so an unannounced release still gets sane limits. On OpenAI, an "off" effort level simply omits the reasoning parameter rather than sending an unsupported value; Bedrock maps it to its native "none".

The assistant monorepo pins this commit in a companion PR that adds pricing, model-picker placement, and cost multipliers on the consumer side.

title: Coalesce concurrent identical model-discovery requests
description:
When the same backend is configured under two provider entries — say the built-in provider plus a custom entry pointing at one gateway, or two custom entries on one server — hosts launch all provider model fetches in parallel, producing identical concurrent requests. This PR extends the registry-owned, in-flight-only request coalescer from LiteLLM to every provider whose discovery is a single GET: openai-compatible, openai, ollama, lmstudio, openrouter, anthropic, deepseek, and gemini. A second call with the same request identity — operation namespace, HTTP method, normalized URL, and a fingerprint of the auth and response-affecting headers — joins the in-flight request instead of starting a new one. Each joiner parses and labels its own results from the shared decoded payload, so per-provider behavior is unchanged.

Coalescing is deliberately conservative. Requests that differ in URL, method, headers, or credentials never share. A call made after a provider's cache is cleared never joins a flight started before the clear, so a retry always gets a fresh answer. Failures and timeouts are never retained, and settlement removes entries identity-safely, so no disposal API is needed. Raw secrets are never used as map keys or logged — the header fingerprint is a SHA-256 hash, implemented in pure TypeScript so the browser bundle keeps working (with known-answer vector tests pinning hash exactness, since the hash keys the identity map).

Two boundaries are worth knowing. Providers that carry a credential in the request URL (Gemini's `?key=` query parameter) keep it out of the coalescer's retained identity key: a new fetcher hook strips the parameter from the identity URL and folds the key into the hashed fingerprint instead. And only the base model-list request joins — a provider's per-model enrichment pass (Ollama's `/api/show` calls) still runs per provider afterward. Providers that own their whole fetch (Portkey's paginated discovery, Databricks) have no base request to coalesce, and singleton-only providers have no duplicate-entry scenario.

The companion PR in the assistant monorepo (branch `fix-provider-hang`) updates the submodule pin to this work; it should merge only after this one lands and the pin is repointed at the merged commit.

title: Add OpenCode provider with Go/Zen selector and session routing
description:
Adds OpenCode support to the provider infrastructure in three parts:

1. Custom providers pointed at OpenCode's Go and Zen endpoints now send a stable per-conversation session header and a host-supplied versioned User-Agent automatically — OpenCode rejects inference requests without them. Every request in a conversation shares the root conversation ID, a new conversation gets a new one, requests to any other provider are unchanged, and a user's explicit headers are never stripped.
2. OpenCode becomes a built-in provider: a single `opencode` provider whose `product` setting (`go` or `zen`, default `zen`) resolves to the corresponding endpoint at catalog build. One workspace key works for both products, and the per-product env vars collapse to `OPENCODE_API_KEY`.
3. The model-discovery cache now keys on the resolved endpoint, so switching products refetches the catalog instead of serving the previous product's list until expiry.

An explicit `baseUrl` still wins over the product default. Resolution also derives an effective-product projection (editable / product-enforced / base-url-override) for hosts to consume, and the configuration watch signature fires on product-only edits so live changes reach running hosts without a restart.

The companion monorepo PR consumes these changes through the updated submodule pin.

title: Add the OpenCode provider and a default User-Agent for direct providers
description:
# Add built-in OpenCode provider with session routing and protocol-aware model routing

This PR adds OpenCode Go and Zen support to the provider bridge and configuration schema, so host applications (Posit Assistant across Positron, standalone, RStudio, and the TUI) can offer OpenCode as a built-in provider entry with a Go/Zen product selector instead of requiring hand-configured custom providers. The default product is Go, the subscription offering; the chosen product is stored as a product setting in the provider configuration rather than as a URL, so endpoint addresses stay owned by the library.

The built-in OpenCode provider applies the session header OpenCode requires: each chat request builds its protocol delegate with the conversation's root ID in the session header, so every request in a conversation carries the same identity and a new conversation gets a new one. A user's own configured headers are never stripped — the generated session value wins over a conflicting hand-set header — and conversations without a root conversation ID simply omit the header, leaving a hand-set one untouched. Because the header is owned by the provider rather than matched on request URLs, requests to any other provider are untouched and custom providers pointed at OpenCode endpoints do not receive it; the built-in provider is the supported path.

Built-in OpenCode models are routed over the wire protocol each model documents — Responses, Anthropic Messages, Chat Completions, or Google's generateContent — rather than all going over Chat Completions, which could produce a generic HTTP 500 from OpenCode for models documented on a different endpoint. A shared routing table in the config package drives protocol selection for all clients, a user's own routing overrides still win, and probe-verified capability information is kept separate from documented routing defaults so a probe result on one model can't silently re-route the whole catalog. Models without a documented protocol keep the previous default behavior.

The configuration schema gains a product field for the OpenCode provider, a single `OPENCODE_API_KEY` environment variable (one OpenCode workspace key works for both products), and the product-aware endpoint resolution behind the selector.

title: Fix Bedrock HTTP 400 for gpt-5.6-sol by using auto reasoning summary
description:
When a host application chats with a GPT 5.6-series model through Amazon Bedrock's OpenAI Responses route (for example, `openai.gpt-5.6-sol`), every request fails with `HTTP 400: Unsupported parameter: 'reasoning.summary' is not supported with the 'openai.gpt-5.6-sol' model.` This started suddenly with no change on the client's side: Bedrock began rejecting the explicit reasoning-summary level (`concise`/`detailed`) the client sends on that route.

This PR sends `auto` — the OpenAI Responses API's own default — instead of an explicit level. Bedrock accepts `auto` for these models, and the route never returned reasoning-summary text either way, so the only visible change is that requests succeed again.

Only the Bedrock OpenAI Responses route changes. The Bedrock chat route, Anthropic and Converse routes, and every other provider are untouched. If Bedrock's validation later tightens further and rejects the field entirely, omitting it is the remaining fallback.

## Verification

The Mantle routing test now asserts the `auto` level, and the change was confirmed against the live `openai.gpt-5.6-sol` model: requests complete and stream a response instead of returning HTTP 400.

title: Support auth-less custom Anthropic providers via apiKeyOptional
description:
This PR lets a custom Anthropic provider in `providers.json` be used without an API key, via a new optional `apiKeyOptional: true` field. The motivating case is an endpoint that handles authentication itself — for example, a local enterprise proxy that injects SSO credentials — so asking the user for a key is unnecessary (reported in posit-dev/assistant-feedback#91).

Custom OpenAI-compatible entries already worked this way. Custom Anthropic entries always required a key, which made this kind of proxy impossible to configure.

## How it works

**Deciding whether a key is required.** A provider is key-optional if its provider type is inherently key-optional (as OpenAI-compatible already is) OR the individual entry sets `apiKeyOptional: true`. Like other `providers.json` settings, the field can come from the user's config file or from admin-managed default/enforced config, so an administrator can pin the policy fleet-wide.

Each resolved catalog entry records both the effective policy and where it came from (built-in default, admin default, user config, or admin-enforced). Consumers need this to tell an overridable default apart from an enforced value, even when the two happen to be equal. Editing only this field in `providers.json` triggers a live reload: the file watcher treats it as a connection change, so the provider is re-registered and its credentials are re-resolved without a restart.

**What "no key" means on the wire.** When the policy is on, an empty API key string is the signal for "send no credentials":

- Model discovery sends only the `anthropic-version` header — no auth headers.
- Chat needs care because the Anthropic SDK falls back to the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable when given an empty key. We hand the SDK a non-empty placeholder to prevent that, then strip both `x-api-key` and `Authorization` from the request before it is sent (and before raw HTTP logging captures it). Neither a real key nor the placeholder ever reaches the endpoint or the log files.

## Changes

- `providers.json` schema: the custom Anthropic variant, and the admin default/enforced fragment shape, now accept `apiKeyOptional`; the generated JSON schema is regenerated.
- Resolved catalog entries now carry the effective key-optionality policy and its source; the catalog builder copies both for custom entries.
- The config file watcher treats a policy-only edit as a connection change, triggering a live reload.
- New auth-descriptor helper that combines the provider-type default with the entry's authored value; the existing type-level map is unchanged for back-compat.
- Anthropic model discovery and chat accept an empty key as described above.

## Testing

- Wire-level tests assert that no auth header reaches the endpoint or the raw request logs, including with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set in the test process to prove it isn't inherited.
- The generated-schema equality test passes.

This supports the auth-less custom provider feature in posit-dev/assistant; the companion Positron change (teaching the host's own provider management about the new field) is specced separately.

title: Remove the obsolete OAuth fallback
description:
Applications that authenticate through ai-lib now use one OAuth sign-in and refresh path. The removed fallback was unreachable in current applications, but it retained older error handling that could clear stored tokens after any refresh failure.

Store-backed backends continue to acquire and refresh OAuth credentials through the current flow. Host-owned credential backends still resolve their own credentials; when a backend has no OAuth acquisition support, direct token and sign-in compatibility calls return no token or report that OAuth sign-in is unsupported instead of starting a second controller.

## Breaking changes

The library no longer exposes the legacy OAuth backend extension. Any external consumer that provided it must migrate to the current OAuth acquisition hooks; in-repository consumers already use those hooks.

title: Keep stored OAuth tokens through transient refresh failures
description:
When a network blip interrupts a token refresh, the apps built on this library (the Posit Assistant standalone app, RStudio integration, and Canvas) sign the user out of Posit AI Pass — and any other OAuth device-flow provider — until they re-authenticate by hand. Any refresh error did this: a dropped connection, a timeout, a 429 or 5xx from the auth server. The stored tokens were deleted, the credential was marked permanently failed, and nothing retried, so every launch showed signed-out. User logs show this happening on ordinary network errors.

This PR narrows token deletion to the one case where re-authentication is genuinely required: a definitive server rejection, meaning an `invalid_grant` or `invalid_client` error code on a 400 or 401 response. Every other failure keeps the stored tokens untouched and retries on a later request, so a transient outage resolves itself instead of logging the user out. A false "transient" verdict now costs a bounded retry; previously a false "terminal" verdict cost the user a manual sign-in.

Supporting changes:

- A 30-second timeout bounds each refresh exchange so a hung request cannot hold the cross-process credential-file lock, and a ~60-second per-process cooldown after a transient failure keeps status polling from hammering the token endpoint during an outage. An expired cooldown is removed before the retry.
- Refresh failure logs now record the classification (terminal or transient), HTTP status, RFC 6749 error code, and the bounded server-supplied detail (for example, "The refresh token expired"). Previously the log kept only the status and code and discarded the detail the response already carried.
- Credential shaping now runs outside the refresh transaction's error boundary. Previously a programming bug in shaping was swallowed and misreported as a lock/IO failure — returning no credentials even after fresh tokens had been committed.

Edge behavior: if a refresh response is lost after the server rotated the token, the preserved old token is already dead and a later retry deletes it via a real `invalid_grant` — rare, and self-correcting into the correct terminal state. Older builds sharing the same credential file can still delete tokens on transient failures; only new builds stop doing so.

## Not included

The legacy OAuth engine path keeps the old delete-on-any-error behavior. No current consumer constructs it (hosts always supply acquisition hooks), and fixing it needs a transaction-scoped persistence primitive its store locking does not yet support.

title: Add Gemini 3.8 Flash support and guard provider tool merges
description:
This PR adds Gemini 3.8 Flash to the Interactions capability profiles and adds a shared guard for attaching provider-defined tools to a request.

Gemini 3.8 Flash gets a thinking profile of low/medium/high — the model rejects "minimal", exactly like 3.7 Flash. The capability rule that previously matched only 3.7 now matches 3.7 and 3.8, so 3.8 inherits the 1M input / 65,536 output limits and the same level set. The generic Gemini 3 rule still governs future models, so unknown IDs keep the fail-open default.

The new merge helper attaches a provider-executed tool (such as Anthropic's or Posit AI's web search) to the outgoing tool map, and rejects the request with a diagnostic naming both tools when a local tool already occupies the key the provider tool needs. Previously the merge silently overwrote the local tool. Both the Anthropic and Posit AI clients now route their web-search merges through the helper, and the helper is the seam the upcoming Gemini Google Search tool will use.

The PR also brings the AI SDK provider family to current versions so this repo's lockfile resolves a single copy of the SDK's core type packages. Previously the OpenAI and Bedrock entries pulled in second copies, and types from different physical copies are incompatible even at matching versions — a latent compile hazard for any future provider-defined tool from those providers. A new CI step checks the lockfile for duplicate copies of those packages and fails with the fix, so the split cannot quietly return. The check looks only at this repo's own lockfile; it knows nothing about consumers.

title: Keep provider credentials resolvable after host environment scrubbing
description:
This PR lets host applications copy provider credential variables at startup and resolve all later credential lookups against that copy, so that a host can delete those variables from its process environment — keeping them away from code it runs on behalf of users, like terminals, scripts, and language runtimes — without losing access to its own providers. Without this, the cleanup breaks the host subtly: providers don't read credentials at startup but when they're needed, so a host that removes the variables at boot doesn't fail at boot — it fails later, the next time a credential is actually read.

The copy works in three parts:

1. Credential lookups that read environment variables can read from the host's copy instead of the live process environment.
2. A single declaration reports which environment variables each provider reads, so the host knows at startup exactly which variables to copy and remove — rather than waiting to see which ones get used.
3. Providers that fetch tokens in the background (Google Vertex, Azure Entra, Foundry) read from the copy, so refreshing an expired token keeps working after the cleanup.

## Example

An operator runs Posit Assistant's multi-user server with Google Vertex configured through `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, the standard Google Cloud variable that points at a service-account file. At startup the server deletes credential variables from its environment so that user-launched terminals and scripts can't see them. Startup looks healthy — nothing has read the variable yet, because the Vertex client only builds its Google Cloud request machinery on first use. When the first model request arrives, the client reaches for `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, finds nothing, and every request fails with an authentication error. Restarting doesn't help; the variable is deleted on every boot.

With this PR, the server copies the variable at startup before deleting it. The Vertex client reads the copy when it builds its request machinery, and requests succeed.

Nothing changes for hosts that don't use this. If no copy is provided, every lookup reads the live process environment exactly as before, and no variables are copied unless the host asks.

## One declaration drives everything (folded in from #102)

The declaration behind part 2 lives in `ai-credentials` and is the single owner of every environment variable a provider's credential layer or SDK reads. Each field is an `EnvironmentFieldDescriptor { name, scrub }`, and that one declaration drives three consumers that previously kept their own copies of these names:

- env credential resolution (`resolveCredentialsFromEnv`),
- the host's capture and scrub partitions (`captureProviderEnvironment` returns `declaredNames` plus the `scrub: true` subset it should delete), and
- a typed `readSdkCredentialEnvironment` reader, which the Vertex and Azure credential constructors consume instead of reading `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` / `AZURE_*` literals — so a renamed or added SDK variable cannot enter capture while being absent from lazy credential construction.

Scrub policy is per-field data: all existing fields keep today's behavior (`scrub: true`), while the non-secret Azure tenant/client IDs are capture-only — copied for lazy SDK construction but deliberately left in the process environment for user code to read.

**Note for external builds:** the bundler alias target narrowed from the whole `providerEnvMappings` module to the registry-data module `providerEnvRegistry` (external variant: an empty registry; the capture/reader implementation is shared by both builds). External consumers' build configs need to alias the new module name.

title: Report GPT-5.6's documented 1M context window as a provider fact
description:
Model capability lookups previously returned a single set of numbers in which provider-published limits and generic fallback defaults were indistinguishable. GPT-5.6 was also capped at 272K — a pricing-tier boundary, not the model's real context window — so consumers could not tell that the model actually accepts roughly 1M tokens of input, and could not distinguish a documented limit from a synthesized one.

This PR separates the two views. Capability inference now returns the provider-published facts alongside the completed operational set, and discovered models carry those facts through resolution. Direct OpenAI GPT-5.6 (Sol, Terra, Luna, and the bare `gpt-5.6` alias) now reports OpenAI's documented 1.05M context window and 128K output maximum; Bedrock Mantle GPT-5.6 reports AWS's documented 1M window, with input and output limits left unknown because AWS does not publish them. Known older releases keep their established windows — GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.5 stay at 272K on Mantle, and the GPT-5 through GPT-5.3 series keep their documented 400K window on direct OpenAI — while unknown future GPT-5.x IDs default optimistically to the family's current-generation window (1M on Mantle, 1.05M on direct OpenAI). User-configured capacity overrides now replace the corresponding facts as well as the operational values, so an override is honored by consumers of either view.

Existing consumers are unaffected: the completed operational set is still returned at top level, so callers that require a number for every field compile and behave unchanged. When a route publishes no limit — for example Mantle's output maximum — the fact view reports it as unknown rather than substituting a generic default, and each corrected capability row carries its primary-source URL and verification date.

This is the ai-lib half of posit-dev/assistant#2321, which consumes these facts to let long GPT-5.6 conversations recover through compaction instead of failing.

title: Fix conversations failing after web search with Anthropic models
description: When a conversation uses a server-side tool such as web search, every subsequent request to an Anthropic-wire model fails with HTTP 400: `web_search_tool_result.tool_use_id: String should match pattern '^srvtoolu_[a-zA-Z0-9_]+$'`. The conversation is stuck — the user cannot continue it until the tool result leaves the request history. The outbound tool-call ID sanitizer added in #52 rewrites IDs that look like duplicates so each request has unique IDs. Its pairing logic assumes a tool result sits in the same message as its call, or in the immediately following one. Server-side tools break that assumption: the SDK places the call in one assistant message and the result in the next, so the sanitizer mistakes the result's ID for a duplicate and appends a dash-based suffix. Dashes are valid for client tool IDs but not for server-minted ones, which must match the stricter pattern Anthropic rejects them against. This PR passes server-minted IDs through untouched. They already satisfy the general ID pattern, they are unique because the server generates them, and no rewrite could produce a valid server ID anyway — sanitizing them can only corrupt the request. Client tool IDs are sanitized exactly as before, so the Kimi-style duplicate handling from #52 is unchanged. Regression coverage replays the observed wire shape — a web search call in one assistant message, its result at the head of the next, with parallel client tool calls interleaved — and fails on the unfixed code with the exact ID corruption seen in production.

title: Declare provider SDK credential environment in ai-credentials
description:
## Summary

Follow-up to #101, addressing its review finding that the environment names a provider's SDK reads lived in three places that must stay in sync (`PROVIDER_ENV_MAPPINGS`, hardcoded `env.AZURE_*` / `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` reads in the bridge, and the host's curated lists).

This PR gives `ai-credentials` a single declaration that drives all three consumers:

- **Uniform field descriptors.** Every mapped field — `apiKey`, each `oauthM2m`/`aws` member, and each SDK member — is now an `EnvironmentFieldDescriptor { name, scrub }`. All existing fields are `scrub: true`, preserving today's behavior exactly (including scrubbing non-secret `AWS_REGION`/`DATABRICKS_HOST` values).
- **`sdkCredentialEnvironment` descriptors**, keyed by the semantic fields of a new `SdkCredentialEnvironment` struct (a misspelled key is a compile error). `google-vertex` declares `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`; `ms-foundry` declares the `AZURE_*` set, with the non-secret tenant/client IDs as capture-only (`scrub: false`) so they stay ambient.
- **Derived capture partitions.** `captureProviderEnvironment` computes `scrubbedNames` vs capture-only names from descriptor flags — no hardcoded split.
- **Typed reader.** `readSdkCredentialEnvironment(env)` assembles the struct via explicit field assignments from the descriptors, so no env-name literal exists outside the declaration. The bridge's `createAzureCredential` and both Vertex sites now consume only this struct; a behavioral test proves every declared semantic key is represented in the reader's result.

Also:

- Guard the `PROVIDER_ENV_MAPPINGS.databricks` dereference for external builds, and mirror the full export surface in `providerEnvMappings-external.ts`, covered by a contract test that aliases the empty variant into the public `/store-backend` surface.
- Collapse the captured-cache double lookup in `createAzureEntraTokenProvider` (WeakMap still keyed on the raw captured record).
- Regression tests for previously uncovered branches: explicit `tenantId` overriding captured `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, certificate construction with password forwarding, incomplete captured values falling back to `DefaultAzureCredential`, and a `registerAllProviders`-level test that `credentialEnvironment` reaches both the google-vertex and ms-foundry registrar closures.

## Test plan

- `npm run test`, `npm run check-types`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` in ai-lib — all pass (571 tests).
- Monorepo follow-up (host slimming, pin update) lands separately after this merges.

The picker now shows them with Anthropic's official display names, and there is one less list to keep in sync by hand.

The supplemental-list mechanism itself stays in place for future models the API doesn't return yet, with a commented-out Claude Fable 5.1 entry marking the spot. Fable 5.1 is deliberately not listed manually for now: once Anthropic's endpoint returns it, it appears in the picker automatically. If the endpoint ever stops returning one of these models, that model disappears from the picker rather than lingering as a stale manual entry.

Capability inference for `claude-fable-5-1` is already covered by the existing Fable prefix rule (1M context window, 128k max output, always-on adaptive thinking with effort levels low through max), and a new test pins that mapping so the model gets correct limits the moment it shows up — regardless of how it enters the catalog.

title: Rename the Posit AI subscription to Posit AI Pass
description:
Follows posit-dev/assistant#2295, which renamed the managed model subscription to "Posit AI Pass" so it reads distinctly from the wider Posit AI effort. This is the `ai-lib` half, listed there as a follow-up.

34 occurrences across comments, README tables, the explainer page, test descriptions, and two runtime error messages.

## User-visible changes

Two error messages, both of which can reach the Assistant chat UI:

| Message | Site | How it is reached |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Unsupported protocol for Posit AI Pass: <protocol>` | `PositAiClient.ts:296` | A per-model `protocol` override in `providers.json`. Four of the six `PROTOCOL_VALUES` (`openai-responses`, `mlflow-responses`, `bedrock-converse`, `google-generative`) have no branch in `PositAiClient`, which handles `anthropic-messages` and `openai-chat`. Throws at chat time. |
| `Posit AI Pass provider requires OAuth credentials, got: <type>` | `positai-provider.ts:227` | Non-OAuth credentials for `positai`. There is no `positai` entry in `providerEnvMappings.ts`, so this needs a hand-edited credential store or a host passing the wrong shape. |

The first is unreachable through model discovery: `mapProtocol()` emits only the two handled values and returns `undefined` otherwise, so the client falls back to model-ID inference. It fires only on explicit user configuration.

Nothing in the assistant repo string-matches either message, so the pin bump does not break error handling there.

Everything else in this PR is comments, test descriptions, README tables, and memory-bank docs. `docs/explainer.html` also changed, but the package ships `files: ["dist"]` and nothing references that file, so it is repo-local.

## Deliberately unchanged

- **The `positai` provider ID and code identifiers** (`PositAiClient`, `POSIT_AI_DEFAULTS`, `positaiLogin`). These are persisted in `providers.json` and the credential store.
- **Four family-sense references**, which name the product family sharing `~/.posit/ai/` rather than the subscription, matching that PR's decision to keep "Posit AI products":
  - the `providers.json` schema title and its generator in `generate-schema.ts:207`
  - the `ai-credentials` package description
  - the credential-store path comment in `store/defaults.ts:8`

The schema title is the one worth calling out, since editors show it in `providers.json` tooltips. It titles the whole document — whose top-level properties are `$schema`, `providers`, and `version` — not the `positai` block. Renaming it would tell users that a file holding Anthropic, OpenAI, and Bedrock config is "Posit AI Pass".

## Verification

- `npm run build` — passes
- `npm run test` — 1208 passing, empty stderr
- `npm run format:check` — clean
- `npm run lint` — clean
- Workspace `check-types` — passes for all three packages
- Shape guard (`typechecks/`) — passes
- `providers.schema.json` regenerates unchanged

Two pre-existing issues found along the way, neither addressed here:

- `npm run check-types` cannot finish from the repo root. Its last step is `tsc -p typechecks/tsconfig.json`, but root `devDependencies` are husky, lint-staged, and oxfmt only, with no `typescript` hoisted to root `node_modules`. After a clean `npm ci` it exits 127 on `sh: tsc: command not found`. The shape guard was run via `packages/ai-config/node_modules/.bin/tsc`.
- `watch-catalog.test.ts > should include the full catalog in change events` is load-sensitive. It timed out at 5000ms during one full-suite run; on a clean `main` the same test passes but takes 4617ms.

## Follow-up

Consuming this requires a `packages/ai-lib` submodule pin bump in the assistant repo, which is not part of this change.

title: Add opt-in raw HTTP request/response logging
description:
Adds a fetch wrapper (`raw-http-logging.ts`) that captures byte-faithful `.http` request/response pairs for wire-level debugging of provider rejections — the AI SDK-structured `JsonRequestLogger` view in the monorepo shows the SDK's interpretation of a call, not the actual bytes on the wire, which is exactly what you need when a provider returns a 400 you can't explain.

## Behavior

- **Opt-in and dynamic.** Logging is active while the configured `raw-http/` directory exists — late binding, checked per chat call, so you can `mkdir` mid-session to enable capture without a restart. `PA_RAW_HTTP_LOG_DIR` turns it on unconditionally.
- **Redaction.** Credential-bearing header values are redacted; bodies are always byte-for-byte.
- **Never breaks a request.** All logging errors are swallowed.
- **Bundle-safe.** `node:fs` is looked up lazily via `process.getBuiltinModule` rather than a static `node:` import, so the module can be bundled into the Positron webview frontend (which shares chunks with the model clients). Outside Node, logging simply disables itself.

Wired into every AI SDK-backed model client — OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Gemini, Vertex, Ollama, OpenRouter, Posit AI, Snowflake, Bedrock — composing with each client's existing custom-fetch wrappers rather than replacing them.

## Consumer

Needed by posit-dev/assistant#2015, which pins this branch and adds the per-deployment `raw-http/` log directories plus the `rawHttpLogging.md` memory-bank doc. That PR can't merge until this one does.

title: Let the store credential backend run on any key-value storage
description:
The store-backed credential backend no longer requires the file-based credential store. It now accepts any storage backing that provides four operations — read a key, write a key, run a function under a lock, and watch for changes — so hosts with their own secure storage can serve credentials through it directly.

The motivating case is Posit Assistant's Positron extension, which keeps Assistant-managed provider credentials in VS Code's OS-keychain-encrypted SecretStorage rather than the shared credentials file. Previously that required either duplicating the backend's credential policy or routing secrets through the file store; now only the key-value backing is injected, and all policy — readiness normalization, environment-variable fallback, keyless-provider handling, and tombstone clears — stays in the backend.

There is no behavior change for existing consumers: the current file store satisfies the new storage contract structurally, so existing call sites compile and run unchanged.

One contract matters for anyone implementing a custom backing: the lock must exclude every writer of the same keys, because OAuth token acquisition and AWS preserve-mutations are read-modify-write transactions. A backing that can only offer weaker exclusion — an in-process mutex over a per-window secret store, for example — is safe only for configurations limited to whole-record API-key replace and clear, with no OAuth or AWS providers. This constraint is documented on the interface itself.

## Changes

- The backend's store option is retyped from the concrete file store to a narrow structural interface covering exactly the four operations it consumes. Previously, providing non-file storage meant forking the backend's credential policy.
- The backend module no longer imports the file-store module at all, so the generic file key-value store stays free of credential-backend contracts. Previously the dependency ran the other way.
- The new interface is exported from `ai-credentials/store-backend` alongside the backend factory, and the memory-bank docs are updated to match.

## Verification

- `npm run check-types` in this repo: the existing file store is passed to the backend unchanged, so a structural mismatch would fail compilation.
- Consumers can confirm the seam by passing a minimal in-memory object with `get`/`set`/`withLock`/`watch` and observing identical credential resolution behavior.

title: Add transformSource hook for counterfactual catalog queries
description:
A consumer that needs to answer "what would the resolved catalog look like without this configuration layer?" has no way to ask it. The Posit Assistant monorepo's Bedrock disconnect flow needs exactly this: when environment variables or admin configuration would keep a provider connected after the user's own settings are cleared, the clear action must say so — but answering meant re-implementing source precedence by hand, which drifts from the real loader.

`loadProviderCatalogReport` now accepts an optional `transformSource` hook that is applied to every loaded source (file, environment fragments, legacy settings) before resolution. A counterfactual query reuses the exact source options of the live load — same paths, environment variables, and legacy channels — and simply rewrites the sources in flight.

The hook is load-path only; watch paths never apply it. This PR also updates the memory-bank guidance on `BEDROCK_DEFAULTS`: credential synthesis in the monorepo no longer applies the implicit `us-east-1` fallback (synthesis is now gated on catalog auth readiness, which requires deliberate region configuration), and adding Bedrock to the defaults map would now make every install fetch Bedrock models.

Consumed by the assistant monorepo's AWS sign-in branch (https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/2243), which uses the hook for its clear-confirmation counterfactual.

title: Re-export CredentialConfigTarget and StructuredBaseUrlSource from credential-shaping

title: Rename connect provider to posit-connect, export integrations read
description:
Two problems with the built-in Connect provider that shipped in #81. First, its provider id `connect` collides with the generic "connect a provider" vocabulary in host UIs (notably Positron), so logs, schema keys, and model ids read ambiguously. Second, a host application that wants to validate a Connect configuration — for example Posit Assistant's Test button in the AI Providers dialog — had to re-implement the integrations-endpoint read (path, `Authorization: Key` convention, response validation), duplicating logic that must stay in sync with discovery.

This PR renames the provider id, client kind, schema key, env-mapping keys, and the minted model-id prefix from `connect` to `posit-connect`, so the product is named unambiguously everywhere (models now appear as `posit-connect-<slug>-<guid>/<modelId>`). It also promotes the private integrations fetch into an exported `fetchConnectIntegrations` helper that fetches, validates, and shapes allowlisted integrations, so discovery and host test probes share one canonical read of the endpoint instead of drifting apart. Regression tests now cover both env dispatch keys under the renamed id: `CONNECT_API_KEY` through the ai-credentials env resolver and `POSIT_CONNECT_URL` through ai-config's connection-env layer into the resolved catalog.

Compatibility is preserved where it matters: the provider is experimental and unreleased, so there are no stored credentials or stamped model ids to migrate, and the environment variable names stay `CONNECT_API_KEY` and `POSIT_CONNECT_URL`. Error reporting improves slightly — HTTP failures from the integrations endpoint now include the status text — and unsupported integration templates continue to be skipped with a warning rather than failing discovery.

## Verification

- `connect-provider.test.ts` covers the rename (minted prefixes, log tags) and the exported helper's validation and shaping.
- New tests assert `CONNECT_API_KEY` resolves through the env credential resolver and `POSIT_CONNECT_URL` flows into the resolved catalog under the `posit-connect` id.
- The Posit Assistant monorepo pins this branch and compiles, typechecks, and tests cleanly against it.

Bedrock's base-URL honoring gets its own routing tests.
