description:
## Summary

Two API changes in `ai-credentials` so a host can resolve credentials for `providers.custom` entries: entries the user names themselves, which come and go while the process is running. Nothing changes for built-in providers.

For https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/13823, https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/12747, https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/issues/14141. Consumed by posit-dev/positron#15675 and posit-dev/assistant#2170.

Merge this first, then bump the ai-lib submodule in posit-dev/assistant#2170.

## What changes

### 1. `PositronBackend` takes a provider-map getter instead of a table

`createPositronBackend({ providerMap })` used to take a `ProviderMap` read once at construction. It now takes `() => ProviderMap`.

Built-in providers are a fixed table, so reading it once was fine. Custom entries aren't: the ids are the user's chosen names, and adding, deleting, or disabling one in `providers.json` changes the map mid-session. With a captured table, anything added after the backend was built resolves to nothing and never fires a credential-change event, with no signal saying why.

Two things follow from that: `getCredentials` looks its mapping up per call, and the auth-provider-id → provider-id reverse lookup happens per session-change event rather than from an index built at construction.

### 2. A registration that lands mid-lookup can't poison the "not registered" verdict

Existing behaviour: when `getSession` rejects with "provider not registered", the backend remembers that and skips future silent lookups, because the rejection takes several seconds to arrive.

That window is long enough for the provider to register while a lookup is still in the air. The `onDidChangeSessions` event lands first and clears the verdict, then the stale rejection lands and re-installs it. The provider is now unresolvable for the rest of the process and no further event is coming to fix it. That is exactly the ordering you hit when a custom entry is added, or first loaded, at the same time its auth provider registers.

Fix: count registration signals per auth provider. A lookup records the count it started under, and only caches its verdict if the count hasn't moved.

### 3. `CredentialConfig` reads now say which provider they are for

`getBaseUrl` and `getCustomHeaders` took a bare `configKey` string; `getAws`, `getSnowflake`, and `getDatabricks` took no arguments at all. All five now take `CredentialConfigTarget = { providerId, configKey }`, and `shapeCredentials` gains a leading `providerId`.

Neither old form can name a custom entry:

- `configKey` is a settings namespace, not an identity, and it isn't unique. `snowflake-cortex` derives the configKey `snowflake`, which is itself a legal custom entry name, so a reader keying on configKey hands a custom entry the built-in's connection.
- The no-argument getters assume one provider per credential type, which was true when only `bedrock` could be AWS. A custom `type: "aws"` entry would inherit bedrock's region.

`providerId` can't collide, because custom entry names reserve every built-in id (enforced on the Positron side). Catalog-backed adapters answer from `providerId`; settings-backed adapters keep reading `authentication.<configKey>.*`. It's one object rather than two string parameters so the two can't be transposed silently.

### 4. `structuredBaseUrl` on the mapping

Some apikey providers build their base URL from structured connection fields instead of a flat `baseUrl`: Snowflake from host or account, Databricks from workspace host. Shaping picked those out with `authProviderId === "snowflake-cortex"`, which a user-named entry never matches, so a `type: "snowflake"` custom entry quietly fell through to the flat-baseUrl path.

`AuthProviderMapping` gets an optional `structuredBaseUrl: "snowflake" | "databricks"`. Built-ins keep their derivation through a small table keyed by auth provider id, so hosts that hand-build mappings for built-ins don't need updating.

One deliberate behaviour change here: Snowflake now falls back to a flat `baseUrl` when there is no host or account. Structured fields still win, so a stale URL can't shadow them, but the flat form has to resolve too. It's what standalone's Add-custom-provider form writes in custom-URL mode, it's the only shape that can express a non-standard Cortex path, and the other hosts already honour it (`conn.baseUrl ?? derive(conn)`).

## Callers

Both are breaking signature changes. The consumer PRs land the updates and should merge alongside this one:

- posit-dev/positron#15675 — renderer `CredentialConfig` adapter and the `createPositronBackend` call
- posit-dev/assistant#2170 — catalog-backed `CredentialConfig`, plus a mapping per enabled custom entry

## Tests

`PositronBackend`:
- a custom entry resolves, and fires a credential change for its auth provider
- an entry that appears after the backend was built still notifies
- a provider registering mid-lookup doesn't get its verdict cached

`shapeCredentials`:
- structured fields beat a flat `baseUrl`, and a flat `baseUrl` resolves when there are no structured fields
- a custom entry gets its own AWS region, its own Cortex host, and its own flat `baseUrl`
- an entry named `snowflake` isn't confused with the built-in `snowflake-cortex`

title: Support Microsoft Foundry authentication with Entra ID
description:
Microsoft Foundry connections currently require an API key, so organizations that disable key-based authentication cannot use their deployments. This change lets the built-in Microsoft Foundry provider use Microsoft Entra ID instead, acquiring and refreshing tokens through Azure CLI credentials, managed identity, workload identity, or an environment service principal. API-key authentication remains the default for existing configurations. If Azure credentials are unavailable, users receive an actionable message that directs them to run `az login`; token providers remain separate for different tenants and scopes.

## Changes

- Microsoft Foundry connections can select API-key or Entra ID authentication. Previously, all connections required an API key.
- Entra mode acquires tokens at request time and stores no secret material. Previously, the provider had no keyless authentication path.
- Applications can identify which Foundry connection fields come from user, administrator, environment, or default configuration. This lets configuration screens keep administrator-managed fields read-only without disabling fields users still control.
- Custom Microsoft Foundry providers continue to require API keys; Entra mode applies only to the built-in provider.

## Breaking changes

The Azure SDK dependencies require Node.js 22.12 or later. Consumers using an older Node.js release must upgrade before adopting this version.

Related to https://github.com/posit-dev/positron/discussions/15663

title: Extend the auth-attempt contract for credential refresh
description:
Consumers that refresh expired credentials (for example AWS SSO or Google ADC) can't express two common outcomes with the current attempt contract: a refresh that finishes synchronously with no user interaction, and a refresh that can't be attempted at all in the current environment. They also can't represent a login flow whose browser step is owned by an external process like a spawned CLI. Callers have to fake these cases with errors or side channels.

This PR extends the authentication contract in `ai-credentials` with three additions. A new `external-browser` challenge kind describes a flow where an external process (such as `gcloud`) owns the browser step, with display instructions and an optional URL. A `completed` start result covers synchronous refreshes — such as a silent token refresh — that create no attempt and just tell the caller to refetch auth status. An `unavailable` start result with a reason covers cases where no attempt can be created (missing CLI, no SSO profile, no reachable browser), so the caller can fall back to a configuration UI.

All additions are new union members, so existing consumers compile and behave unchanged. The new contract is covered by attempt-contract tests.

## Changes

- `AuthenticationChallenge` gains an `external-browser` kind for flows where a spawned process owns the browser step. Previously, only interactive URL-based challenges could be expressed.
- `AuthenticationStartResult` gains `completed` and `unavailable` statuses. Previously, a start call could only report `started` or `already-in-progress`, leaving no way to express synchronous success or environment-level unavailability.

title: Fix process.send call to compile against all @types/node 22.x
description:
## Problem

`lock-holder.ts` called `process.send("lock-released", () => resolve())`, which relies on the `send(message, callback)` overload. That overload was only added to `@types/node` in 22.19.x; 22.18.x has just the 4-arg form where the second parameter is a `SendHandle`.

Consumers pinned to `@types/node` 22.18.x (e.g. the assistant monorepo's root lockfile) fail to compile `ai-credentials` during the postinstall build:

```
src/store/__tests__/helpers/lock-holder.ts(45,33): error TS2345:
  Argument of type '() => void' is not assignable to parameter of type 'SendHandle'.
```

This surfaced as a CI failure on posit-dev/assistant#2199 that wasn't locally reproducible, because a stale `packages/ai-lib/node_modules` (installed from this repo's own lockfile, which pins 22.19.21) shadowed the monorepo's hoisted 22.18.13.

## Fix

Use the 4-arg overload explicitly — it exists in both versions:

```ts
process.send("lock-released", undefined, undefined, () => resolve());
```

Verified: the original code fails with the exact CI error when compiled against 22.18.13, and the fixed code compiles against both 22.18.13 and 22.19.21.

title: Stop Posit AI models from truncating long replies at 4,096 tokens
description:
When you chat with a Posit AI model that doesn't declare its own output limit — GLM 5.2 today — a long reply cuts off mid-thought at exactly 4,096 tokens. The assistant never tells the server how much output to allow, so the server's small default applies and the response ends with a "length" stop reason.

The assistant now sends a default limit of 16,384 output tokens for every Posit AI model, matching the baseline it already uses for other providers. Models that declare their own limit, such as Kimi K3 at 131,072, keep it.

If a model is new or otherwise unknown to the assistant, the 16,384 default applies instead of the server's. No server changes are required. The new value takes effect on the next model-list refresh; cached model lists refresh within an hour.

title: Speed up ai-lib tests and improve failure diagnostics
description:
AI library test runs spend most of their time waiting on fixed watcher delays, which slows local and CI feedback and can hide synchronization failures. This change waits for watcher readiness and observed events, centralizes exact filesystem and request-capture setup, and gives equivalent provider cases independent failure names. Disposal and no-event checks retain bounded quiet periods, real atomic file replacement and cross-process lock contention remain covered, and generated provider-schema drift now fails a test.

## Changes

- Watcher tests now synchronize with readiness and delivered events instead of fixed startup and delivery sleeps, while real filesystem and process integration remains covered.
- Configuration, credential-store, and raw HTTP request tests now share narrow fixtures without normalizing authored files, stored bytes, URLs, headers, or request bodies.
- Mutation, provider-classification, and protocol-routing tests now live beside the behavior they cover, so failures identify the responsible area.
- Equivalent capability and provider-routing cases now run as independently named rows instead of opaque loops.
- The checked-in provider schema now has a byte-for-byte parity test against generated output.

## Verification

- Ran all default tests three times with 1,070 tests across 83 files and no stderr output.
- Ran type checks, formatting checks, bridge lint, all package builds, and the 35-test build-coordinator suite.
- Reduced median grouped test time from 24.38 seconds to 10.25 seconds; the configuration watcher suite fell from 15.38 seconds to 4.63 seconds, and the credential-store suite fell from 5.01 seconds to 1.66 seconds.

title: Testing updates
description: This PR makes some small changes to help support https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/2188

title: Show actionable errors for misconfigured OAuth auth hosts
description:
When a user writes the Posit AI sign-in host as a full URL in `providers.json` (for example `https://login.posit.cloud` instead of `login.posit.cloud`), device sign-in fails with `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND https` — a DNS error for the literal hostname "https" that says nothing about the real mistake. And when the sign-in server rejects a request (for example, a client ID that doesn't belong to that environment), the thrown error is only `oauth_http_400`, discarding the response body that names the actual problem. Users hit a wall in both cases and can't tell whether the fault is their config, their network, or the service.

With this PR, both failures explain themselves. A host containing a URL scheme or path is rejected when the sign-in endpoints are built, with a message that names the expected format: `Invalid auth host "https://login.posit.cloud": expected a bare hostname such as "login.posit.cloud" — remove the URL scheme and any path.` Server rejections now include the response body — the standard OAuth error description when present, otherwise the raw body, bounded — so a wrong client ID surfaces as `oauth_http_400: Invalid client_id parameter value.` instead of a bare status.

Fallback behavior is unchanged: a correctly formatted host works exactly as before, and if an error response has no readable body, the error falls back to the status-only form (`oauth_http_400`).

## Design decisions

A scheme-carrying host is rejected with a descriptive error rather than silently corrected. Silent normalization would also work, but accepting two formats for one setting makes configuration harder to reason about and harder to validate; a clear error teaches the expected format at the moment it matters.

## Not included

The UI-side handling of these errors (showing the cause chain, tailoring the failure dialog, letting users clear a recorded failure) lives in the assistant monorepo, which consumes this change via its submodule pin.

title: Add wire tests for classifier cache-breakpoint shapes
description:
Adds wire-level tests in `ai-provider-bridge` covering the exact cache-breakpoint marker shapes that the assistant monorepo's auto-mode permission classifier sends (posit-dev/assistant#2159). The classifier splits its user message into per-entry content blocks and places cache breakpoints on the system prompt, a read anchor, and the current end; these tests pin the serialized request bodies so the bridge keeps emitting the shapes the classifier's prompt caching depends on.

## Changes

- `anthropic-cache-breakpoint-wire.test.ts`: asserts `cache_control` lands on the system block and the first user content block only, with no `bedrock`/`openai` namespace leakage, for both the Anthropic Messages API and Bedrock InvokeModel serializers.
- `openai-explicit-prompt-caching-wire.test.ts`: classifier-shape cases for the OpenAI Responses and Chat serializers, asserting the explicit breakpoint lands after the stable transcript prefix only.
- Updates the existing classifier wire fixtures for the block-split read-anchor shape and matches the OpenAI fixture to the full marker shape.

Test-only change; no runtime behavior affected.

title: Bound cached model discovery with a configurable 15s deadline
description:
`createCachedModelFetcher()` — the shared fetcher behind direct-provider model discovery — previously let the base request, provider-owned `fetchFresh`, and enrichment run with no timeout, so a hung provider endpoint (VPN, proxy, sleeping local server) could stall model discovery indefinitely. This adds a configurable `discoveryDeadlineMs` option beside `ttl`, defaulting to 15 seconds (`DEFAULT_DISCOVERY_DEADLINE_MS`), and threads an `AbortController` signal through the request `fetch`, `fetchFresh`, and `enrichModels`. The whole fresh-discovery operation is raced against the deadline, so even a callback that ignores cancellation releases the caller.

Timeout preserves the existing fresh → stale-cache → static-fallback behavior, and a timed-out or late operation never overwrites a newer cache generation (a generation guard bumped by `clearCache()` covers the in-flight case). Portkey's paginated catalog fetch and Ollama's capability enrichment propagate the signal through their nested requests.

The 15s default matches the Node model service's existing per-provider envelope, so consumers keep their current behavior; shorter deadlines are an explicit per-surface policy.

## Verification

New fake-timer tests in `cached-model-fetcher.test.ts` cover the 15s default and explicit deadlines, request/fetchFresh/enrichment timeouts, stale-cache fallback on timeout, late settlement, timer cleanup, and cache clearing during an in-flight fetch; Portkey and Ollama suites cover signal propagation. Bridge suite: 450 tests passing. Consumer-side coverage lives in the assistant monorepo (posit-dev/assistant), whose submodule pin update references this change.

title: Remove `PlatformBaseline` from provider catalog resolution
description:
This PR removes the `PlatformBaseline` (`defaultEnabled` + `providerOverrides`) from ai-config's provider catalog resolution. This existed before because RStudio supported only Posit AI, but that restriction has been removed, and now all platforms support all providers.

Every consumer composes the catalog with `{ defaultEnabled: true }` and no overrides, so the code only added surface area. Now enablement of a provider is decided purely by config layers — enforced, user, legacy Positron, admin default — and a provider no layer mentions is simply enabled.

Note that this will require a change to Positron because it changes the public API.

## Changes

- **ai-config**: `resolveEnabled()` falls back to `true` when no config layer decides; the `baseline` option is removed from `ResolveProviderCatalogOptions`, `LoadCatalogOptions`/`WatchCatalogOptions`, and `buildCatalog`; the `PlatformBaseline` type and export are deleted. Tests that exercised the baseline were updated, and the obsolete "RStudio baseline (positai only)" test was removed.
- **ai-provider-bridge**: the notebooks-consumer smoke test is updated for the new options shape.

## Breaking changes

Downstream consumers passing `baseline` to `resolveProviderCatalog` / `loadResolvedProviderCatalog` / `watchResolvedProviderCatalog` will get a compile-time excess-property error on bump and should delete the option. Known call sites: Positron core's authentication extension (`extensions/authentication/src/providerCatalog.ts`, two sites passing `{ defaultEnabled: true }`) and any Notebooks-style standalone consumer. Runtime behavior is unchanged after adapting, since every known caller passed `defaultEnabled: true`, which is now the hardcoded fallback. The assistant monorepo side is already updated (gitlink bump on the `provider-ui` branch).

title: Add .DS_Store to .gitignore
description: macOS sprinkles `.DS_Store` files through the tree (repo root, `packages/`, `packages/ai-provider-bridge/`), where they show up as untracked noise, including in the submodule checkout inside the Positron repo.

title: Remove low output token limits for Snowflake Cortex models
description: The Snowflake documentation said that Claude and GPT models had a limit of 16k, but we've been told that the documentation is incorrect. This change makes it so that Claude models take maxOutputTokens from the Anthropic capability table and GPT models from the OpenAI table, instead of capping every model at the Cortex REST API's 16,384 per-account default. A conservative 16,384 fallback remains for ids neither upstream table recognizes.

title: Add batch custom provider reader and Snowflake clear provenance
description:
Adds two read-side capabilities to `ai-config` that the Posit Assistant provider-management UI needs to project per-provider management capabilities — whether a user custom provider entry can be deleted, and what clearing a Snowflake connection selection will do — without re-parsing files or mutating state.

**Batch custom provider entry reader.** New `readUserCustomProviderEntries()` (exported from `ai-config/node`) parses the user-layer `providers.json` once and returns every custom provider entry as a `ReadonlyMap`. A missing file yields an empty map; a malformed or unreadable file throws (no salvage). The existing single-entry `readUserCustomProviderEntry()` now delegates to the batch reader, so both share one strict parse path. The assistant's auth-status projection reads this map once per snapshot to decide which custom providers are user-owned and therefore deletable.

**Snowflake selection clear provenance.** `ResolvedConnectionProvenance` gains a `snowflake.connectionName` entry recording whether the effective connection selection is owned by the mutable user layer (`userOwned`) and what the selection would be with all user-layer values removed (`valueAfterUserClear`). This lets the assistant's clear flow predict — before performing a clear — whether removing the user's stored Snowflake selection actually disconnects or leaves a fallback selection from a lower-precedence layer.

Both changes are additive and backward-compatible. Existing Bedrock region provenance behavior is unchanged; its block was only restructured so the Bedrock and Snowflake provenance checks share one function.

## Not included

The consumers of these APIs (auth-status capability projection and the provider accordion UI) live in the assistant monorepo and are in review separately at posit-dev/assistant#2123.

title: Read model capabilities from /v1/models for openai-compatible
description:
These are some proposed changes to support model capabilities for openai-compatible providers. Feel free to adjust the implementation as needed!

The `openai-compatible` provider stamped every model it found with one fixed set: a 128K context window and no image support. That's wrong for plenty of endpoints. A user on an academic endpoint (GWDG SAIA) reported that their models advertise image input and a much bigger window in the `/v1/models` response, but none of it gets read, so the attach button never shows up and the token counter is wrong. This provider exists for endpoints nobody can enumerate ahead of time, so no hardcoded table fixes it: whatever the endpoint says about itself is the only signal available.

Discovery now reads that metadata, best effort. Vision comes from `input`, `architecture.input_modalities`, `architecture.modality`, or `capabilities`. Token limits come from `context_length`, `max_model_len`, `max_context_length`, `max_input_tokens`, and `max_output_tokens`. Each field is checked on its own, and anything missing or malformed falls back to the conservative baseline, so an endpoint that publishes nothing lands exactly where it does today. A `providers.json` `models.overrides` entry still wins over anything read here, so that stays the escape hatch for endpoints that publish nothing or get it wrong.

This still holds up if the built-in `openai-compatible` provider gets deprecated in favour of custom providers only. Both registrars share one model fetcher, and `openai-compatible` is also the generic kind a `providers.custom` entry uses, so the parsing sits on the path that survives. Deprecating would drop one registrar and retarget a test helper, and the custom-endpoint test in here already covers that path.

Addresses https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant-feedback/issues/137, but we'll need to bump ai-lib in positron and posit assistant after this goes in to resolve the issue.

## Implementation choices

Roughly ordered by how much they'd benefit from a second opinion.

1. **Discovery believes what the endpoint says.** A gateway that advertises `image` but rejects image parts turns a greyed-out button into a request error. The trade seems worth it since the metadata is the best signal available and an override can force it back off, but the safer option is leaving capabilities opt-in through config, which fixes nothing for anyone unwilling to hand-write one.

2. **The key list is a union of what four ecosystems publish:** GWDG SAIA, vLLM, LM Studio, and OpenRouter-shaped gateways. It comes from their docs and response shapes, not from testing against live deployments. Anyone who knows what LiteLLM-fronted or Azure-fronted endpoints actually return could add to it.

3. **Bare `max_tokens` is skipped on purpose.** Some endpoints mean the context window by it, others the output ceiling, and guessing wrong quietly corrupts the token counter. The cost is that an endpoint publishing only `max_tokens` gets no window at all.

4. **`supportsToolResultImages` stays `false` even for a vision model.** Images inside tool results are a bigger claim than images in user messages, and with the flag off the host relocates them into a follow-up user message, which works anywhere. This contradicts `openrouter-provider.ts`, which sets the flag to match vision support. One of the two is wrong.

5. **Thinking is not inferred from `output: ["thought"]`,** even though the reporter's endpoint publishes it. Knowing a model can think doesn't say how to ask it to: `thinkingEffortLevels` makes the OpenAI client send `reasoning_effort`, while the reporter's Qwen-on-vLLM models want `chat_template_kwargs`, which `/v1/models` never advertises. Guessing wrong turns a working text chat into a 400. If there's a safe way to detect this, it belongs here.

6. **The image media-type list is assumed, not discovered.** Discovery says whether a model reads images, never which encodings, so `png`/`jpeg`/`gif`/`webp` are hardcoded. `application/pdf` is left out (the OpenAI and Bedrock tables include it) on the grounds that `input: ["image"]` says nothing about PDFs. The constant is also kept local rather than shared with the `ai-config` tables, since the matching lists there are independent table entries. Both could go the other way.

7. **The numeric precedence ladder is invented.** An explicit `max_input_tokens` beats a context-window figure, since a window can include output budget, and a window stands in for the input limit when nothing better is published (matching the DeepSeek path). These fields rarely appear together, so it's mostly theoretical, but it is a guess.

8. **Malformed entries are skipped rather than thrown on.** The old code would throw on a payload with no usable `id`, get swallowed by the fetcher's fallback, and quietly return zero models. Skipping is friendlier, but a badly broken endpoint now fails with a short list instead of loudly.

## Changes

All in `ai-provider-bridge`, one module plus its tests:

- `openai-compatible-provider.ts` normalizes the `/v1/models` entry into a semantic hints object, then merges it over the baseline from `ai-config`'s `inferModelCapabilities`. That deletes the module's own `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_DEFAULTS`, which was a second copy of the same baseline.
- Parsing is cast-free. The old code did `data as { data: Array<{ id: string }> }`, which stops being true the moment remote numbers get believed, so field access goes through small narrowing helpers (`positiveInt`, `stringMembers`, `modalityInputs`) that each take `unknown`. Remote numbers are accepted only as positive safe integers, so a reported `0`, `-1`, `1.5`, or `1e21` can't become a live token limit.
- Tests go through `registry.getModelsForProvider` rather than calling the parser, and cover both registrars. The built-in `registerOpenAICompatibleProvider` had no discovery test at all before this. The parser is kept private rather than exported for tests the way `openrouter-provider.ts` does it, which is easy to change if the exported-parser convention is preferred.

11 of the new tests fail with the provider module reverted. The ones that still pass are the baseline and negative cases, which should hold either way.

## Not included

Audio input, which the issue also asks for. Posit Assistant has no audio path anywhere (no `audio/*` handling in the attachment policy or any capability table), so that's a feature rather than a discovery fix.

## Verification

`npm run check-types`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run test` all pass (966 tests). The consuming monorepo's full suite also passes against this build (8727 tests) with no changes needed on that side.

What hasn't happened is pointing this at a real vision-capable endpoint to confirm the attach button appears and the token counter updates. That's the gap most worth closing before trusting it.

title: Let Posit AI models use per-model output token limits
description: The Posit AI model fetcher applied a blanket `maxOutputTokens: 16000` to every model it returned, which silently capped models that support much larger outputs — Kimi K3, for example, supports up to 131,072 output tokens but was limited to 16,000. This removes the blanket default so each model family declares its own limit in its capability entry (Claude models already do), and models without an entry send no `max_tokens` at all, falling back to the server's per-model default. Kimi K3's Model APIs capability entry now declares its documented 131,072-token limit.

title: Gemini API models: hosted Gemma, 3.6/3.7 Flash, fail-open discovery, raw usage
description:
This PR grew from enabling Gemma into bringing the Gemini API provider up to the current model lineup end to end: hosted Gemma, Gemini 3.6/3.7 Flash, a fail-open discovery posture, profile-derived thinking levels, and raw Interactions usage reporting.

## Hosted Gemma (a937875)

The hosted Gemini API serves Gemma 4 models (`gemma-4-31b-it`, `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`) over the Interactions API, but they never appeared in model discovery: two synchronized gates excluded them — a family-name substring filter in the Gemini model fetcher and the fail-closed Interactions allowlist. Both models are added and verified against the live API (2026-08-17): 256K context / 32K output, binary thinking (`minimal` = off, `high` = on; thinking defaults to ON when the level is omitted), function calling with continuation chaining, image input (png/jpeg/gif/webp), PDF input, tool-result images, and thought summaries.

- The fail-closed Interactions allowlist became the sole eligibility gate; the family-name substring filter is deleted rather than widened, since two synchronized gates caused this bug.
- Interactions profiles generalize from a wire-level `thinkingLevel` list to a product-effort → wire-value mapping (`effortToWireLevel`). Product efforts and wire values are separate vocabularies: for Gemini models the mapping is identity; for Gemma, `off→minimal` (sent explicitly, because Gemma's default is thinking-ON) and `high→high`.
- Behavior change: an unrecognized product effort now omits `thinkingLevel` instead of clamping to `"medium"`. In practice this only affects effort values outside each model's advertised `thinkingEffortLevels`, which core/UI don't send.
- Hosted-Gemma capabilities live in a new Gemini-API-endpoint composition in ai-config (`getGeminiApiModelCapabilities`), routed through `inferModelCapabilities("gemini", …)`. The shared Gemini-family table (also used by provider-agnostic core inference and VS Code LM discovery) and the Posit AI/vLLM Gemma contract (`gemma-helpers.ts`, `off`/`on` via `chat_template_kwargs`) are untouched.
- `buildGeminiModel` consumes the completed `inferModelCapabilities` result and overlays only live `/models` token limits; the bridge-local `GEMINI_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES` fallback is deleted so media/token defaults have a single source of truth.
- Both Gemma models join the static fallback rows used when live discovery fails.

## Gemini 3.6/3.7 Flash and fail-open discovery (793e779, 14f8f6c)

After Gemma, Gemini 3.6/3.7 Flash were the second and third models to be invisible until manually allowlisted, so discovery is now **fail-open** while thinking stays **fail-closed**:

- **Discovery** (`isGeminiApiChatModel`): any chat-shaped model the `/models` endpoint lists may appear in the picker — versioned `gemini-\d`/`gemma-\d` IDs, excluding known non-chat suffixes (`-image`, `-tts`, `-computer-use`) and requiring `generateContent` in `supportedGenerationMethods` when reported (excludes audio/live and embedding models). New models work immediately at their default thinking state; the worst case for a bad inclusion is a visible, retryable error on the first turn.
- **Thinking** (`INTERACTIONS_PROFILES`) stays fail-closed because valid `thinkingLevel` values cannot be inferred — gemini-3.7-flash rejects `minimal` while 3.6-flash accepts it (verified on the live API). Unprofiled models advertise no thinking levels and the client sends no `thinkingLevel`/`thinkingSummaries`.
- Adds verified profiles for `gemini-3.6-flash` (minimal/low/medium/high) and `gemini-3.7-flash` (low/medium/high), plus a matching `gemini-3.7` capability rule in ai-config.

## Thinking levels derived from Interactions profiles (b99612d)

Review follow-ups: `buildGeminiModel` derives advertised `thinkingEffortLevels` from the profile's `effortToWireLevel` keys instead of ai-config's capability table, eliminating two per-model tables that could drift (the picker offering a level the client omits, or hiding one it can send); ai-config's table levels still serve Vertex and other inference consumers. `isInteractionsEligible` is renamed to `hasGeminiInteractionsProfile` since discovery went fail-open and "eligible" no longer describes the predicate.

## Raw Interactions usage persisted (4b44214)

The SDK's interactions provider reports token usage only as `usage.raw` on finish parts; its finish `providerMetadata.google` carries just `interactionId` and `serviceTier`, so hosts that persist finish-step provider metadata (how Anthropic's raw usage reaches disk) silently dropped the raw Gemini usage. `GeminiClient` now hoists `usage.raw` into `providerMetadata.google.usageMetadata` — the same key the generateContent surface populates — on every finish-step part, wrapping outside the expired-ID retry so both attempts are covered. An existing `usageMetadata` is never overwritten. This is what lets the assistant monorepo fix its Gemini cached-token accounting (posit-dev/assistant#2112) and audit Google's cached-token reporting per model.

## Verification

- Regression tests enter through `registerGeminiProvider`/`ProviderRegistry` for discovery, the option-builder mapping tests for thinking levels, and `GeminiClient.chat()` for the raw-usage hoist wiring (fails if the stream wrapper is dropped).
- Full ai-lib suite (475 tests) and typecheck pass; downstream assistant monorepo build, typecheck, and full test suite pass against the head commit.
- End-to-end in the assistant standalone app: Gemma and 3.6/3.7 Flash appear in the picker from live discovery, thinking selectors offer the verified levels, tool-call turns chain via `previous_interaction_id`, and saved conversations now carry the raw Interactions usage (`total_input_tokens`, `total_cached_tokens`, …) on each assistant message.

description: This is similar to https://github.com/posit-dev/assistant/pull/2083. It removes implementation-coupled, duplicative, and scaffolding tests across the main ai-lib packages while retaining coverage of stable behavior, regressions, integration boundaries, and persisted contracts.

title: Normalize block-array `delta.content` on OpenAI-compatible streams
description:
Closes #57

## What this changes

`fixMalformedChunk` in `openai-compat-fetch.ts` gets one more transform. If `delta.content` is an array, the transform makes it a string. The transform keeps the text of `text` blocks and removes `reasoning` blocks.

## Why this file

This file already corrects wire format faults from OpenAI-compatible providers. It holds six such transforms. Transform 4 corrects a similar fault from Snowflake Cortex: an empty `role` value that also fails the Zod check. The new transform is number 7.

The Databricks provider already sends its chat requests through this fetch wrapper. The wrapper already reads the stream on line boundaries, so a `data:` event that spans two network chunks stays safe.

The transform applies to every provider on this path, like its neighbours. An array in `delta.content` is invalid for all of them, so the transform is a no-op elsewhere.

## Why the reasoning text is removed

The OpenAI chat chunk schema has no field for reasoning. Databricks also offers no thinking controls, because `databricks-helpers.ts` removes `thinkingEffortLevels`. An array with no text becomes `""`, and the SDK reads `""` as an empty delta.

The streaming arrays hold only reasoning blocks. The same gateway returns `[reasoning, text]` on its non-streaming path, so the transform keeps `text` blocks.

## Tests

`model-clients/__tests__/openai-compat-fetch.test.ts` is new and holds 7 tests. Five of them fail without this change. The fixtures are real payloads from the gateway.

One test splits a `data:` event across two stream chunks, in the middle of the JSON. This test protects the line buffer. A parser that reads a partial line drops the event and the text after it.

## Verification

The full suite passes: 390 tests in `ai-provider-bridge`, plus 383 and 137 in the other two packages. `npm run check-types` is clean.

A live test against a workspace, with the same client stack the assistant uses:

| Model | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `databricks-gpt-oss-120b` | 12 `AI_TypeValidationError` | 0 errors, correct answer text |
| `databricks-claude-sonnet-5` | fails for some prompts | 0 errors, correct answer text |
| `databricks-claude-opus-5` | fails | 0 errors, correct answer text |

## Scope

This change covers the streaming path only. A non-streaming response holds the same blocks at `choices[].message.content` and never reaches this transform. The assistant always streams.

## Follow-up

The Posit Assistant repository pins `ai-lib` as a submodule. After this pull request merges, the pin needs an update to deliver the fix.

title: Route Databricks models over native vendor APIs
description:
Closes #57.

## Summary

Routes Databricks-served models over their native vendor APIs instead of forcing everything through OpenAI Chat Completions. A per-model `protocol` is stamped at discovery time and each chat request dispatches to a protocol-specific delegate:

| Protocol | Serving base | Gateway base | Who gets it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `anthropic-messages` | `{host}/serving-endpoints/anthropic/v1` | `{host}/ai-gateway/anthropic/v1` | Claude ppt foundation models; external `anthropic`/`bedrock` models |
| `openai-responses` | `{host}/serving-endpoints` | `{host}/ai-gateway/openai/v1` | GPT-5 series / GPT-4o identities only |
| `google-generative` | `{host}/serving-endpoints/gemini/v1beta` | `{host}/ai-gateway/gemini/v1beta` | Gemini endpoints whose *name* identifies the thinking variant (hosted ppt names) and whose entity identities agree with it |
| `openai-chat` (fallback) | `{host}/serving-endpoints` | `{host}/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1` | Everything else |

Native routing recovers what the Chat Completions surface loses today: `thinkingEffortLevels` and (for Claude) explicit cache breakpoints and thinking-block round-trips. Input media types stay masked to images on every route — Databricks documents native passthrough inputs as text/image only ([provider-native API matrix](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/model-serving/provider-native-apis)).

### How it works

- **ai-config**: new `inferDatabricksModelProfile` — pure structural classifier (positive identification per served entity, multi-entity unanimity with conservative capability aggregation, gateway `api_types` gating, first-class `{ excluded }` outcome, explicit `openai-chat` stamp on every fallback path). New `getGeminiGenerateContentProfile` — variant-granular Gemini thinking profiles (2.5 `thinkingBudget` incl. Pro's cannot-disable rule; 3.x `thinkingLevel`), shared by the classifier and the client so stamp and wire choice cannot disagree.
- **Bridge clients**: `AnthropicClient` constructor now takes a discriminated auth config (**breaking change**, see below). New `GeminiGenerateContentClient` — stateless plain-generateContent client (full local history, `thoughtSignature`-based history sanitizer that preserves tool-call signatures, Bearer auth via fetch middleware that strips `x-goog-api-key`).
- **Databricks provider**: per-registration single-flight `ensureSurface` pins the serving-vs-gateway decision for both stamping and routing (probe failure pins serving; `clearCache` resets model cache + surface together, so stamps and routes can never race). One `surface × protocol → base URL` route seam. Client factory is a LiteLLM-style multiplexer over `AnthropicClient` / `OpenAIClient` / `GeminiGenerateContentClient`. `params.baseUrl` from the catalog pipeline is trusted verbatim.

## ⚠️ Breaking change

`AnthropicClient`'s first constructor argument changed from a positional `apiKey: string` to a required discriminated auth config:

```ts
new AnthropicClient({ apiKey: "..." }, baseURL?, customHeaders?, logger?)
new AnthropicClient({ authToken: "..." }, baseURL?, customHeaders?, logger?) // Authorization: Bearer
```

All in-repo call sites are updated. Consumers are source-built (assistant monorepo, Notebooks); the assistant monorepo has no direct `AnthropicClient` usage and typechecks cleanly against this branch.

## ⚠️ Needs verification against a real Databricks workspace

This was developed **without access to a Databricks workspace**. Every unverified value is flagged `PHASE0-VERIFY` in code and degrades safely to `openai-chat` (a wrong guess loses native routing, it does not break a working route). The plan's Phase 0 spikes still need to be run by someone with workspace access — see the testing instructions below.

Unverified assumptions:

1. **Gateway `api_types` strings** for OpenAI and Gemini: guessed as `"openai/v1/responses"` and `"gemini/v1beta/generateContent"` following the shape of the confirmed `"anthropic/v1/messages"`. If wrong, gateway-mode endpoints for those vendors silently stay on `openai-chat`.
2. **Gemini auth**: the client strips `x-goog-api-key` and sends only `Authorization: Bearer`. Unverified that Databricks accepts this.
3. **External-model endpoints**: the `model` body value on native paths is assumed to be the endpoint name.
4. **Bedrock external-provider spelling**: both `bedrock` and `amazon-bedrock` are accepted pending the real enum value.

(Retired: hosted pay-per-token Responses `store` behavior is now documented — `store` / `previous_response_id` [return 400 on ppt models](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/model-serving/query-openai-responses#limitations), so hosted GPT-5 endpoints deliberately don't advertise thinking controls, while external Responses endpoints keep them.)

## Testing instructions (needs a Databricks workspace + PAT)

### Setup

Run the assistant standalone app against this branch:

```bash
# in the posit assistant monorepo
cd packages/ai-lib
git fetch origin databricks-native-protocol && git checkout databricks-native-protocol
cd ../..
npm install && npm run build
npm run dev:standalone
```

Sign in to Databricks in the app (workspace host + personal access token). Watch the server log — the provider logs which surface it pinned (`serving` vs `gateway`) and each fetch URL is visible there for the route checks below.

### 1. Capture discovery responses (resolves assumption 1)

```bash
export H="https://<workspace-host>"; export T="<pat>"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" "$H/api/2.0/serving-endpoints" > serving.json
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" "$H/api/2.0/serving-endpoints:foundation-models" > foundation.json
jq '[.endpoints[].config.served_entities[]?.foundation_model.api_types] | flatten | unique' foundation.json
```

Post the unique `api_types` list (nothing sensitive in it) on this PR. If the OpenAI/Gemini strings differ from the guesses in `packages/ai-config/src/model-capabilities/databricks-helpers.ts` (`DATABRICKS_NATIVE_API_TYPES`), correct the constants. Redacted copies of both JSON files would also make good fixture material.

### 2. Per-protocol chat smokes

For each, confirm the request URL in the server log hits the expected path and the reply streams normally:

- **Claude** (e.g. `databricks-claude-sonnet-4-5`): expect `…/serving-endpoints/anthropic/v1/messages` (serving) or `…/ai-gateway/anthropic/v1/messages` (gateway). Test: plain chat, a tool call, thinking enabled on a model that has effort levels (verify `<thinking>` renders), a multi-turn conversation after a tool call (round-trips thinking blocks), and an image attachment.
- **Gemini hosted ppt** (e.g. `databricks-gemini-2-5-pro`): expect `…/gemini/v1beta/models/<endpoint>:streamGenerateContent`. Test each available variant's thinking control (2.5 Pro must not offer "off"; Flash/Flash-Lite should) and a tool call on a Gemini 3.x model if available (exercises `thoughtSignature` round-trip).
- **GPT-5 hosted ppt** (e.g. `databricks-gpt-5-mini`): expect `…/serving-endpoints/responses` (serving) or `…/ai-gateway/openai/v1/responses` (gateway). Hosted ppt models deliberately expose no thinking controls (Databricks documents `store` as returning 400 there); confirm plain chat and tool calls work on the `/responses` path.
- **External-model endpoints** (if the workspace has any: OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google external models): same checks; also confirms assumption 4. An external GPT-5/4o endpoint with thinking enabled tests the hosted-vs-external Responses split.
- **Any non-native model** (Llama, custom endpoint): expect `…/serving-endpoints/chat/completions` / `…/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/chat/completions` — this is the unchanged fallback path and must keep working.

### 3. Both surfaces

If you have access to workspaces with and without Unity AI Gateway enabled, run step 2 on both. Otherwise note which surface you tested (the log line at startup says which was pinned).

### What "failure" looks like

If a native route errors, the correct short-term mitigation is a per-model or provider-level `protocol: "openai-chat"` override in `providers.json` — please report the model, surface, request URL, and error body here rather than just working around it.

## Follow-up issues

- #62 — per-protocol capability-profile / provenance seam (protocol overrides currently keep stamped capabilities — pre-existing LiteLLM limitation, now documented in `memory-bank/aiConfig.md`).
- #63 — profile-key transport through chat params, if external Gemini endpoints need native routing.

## Verification done without a workspace

- `npm run build`, `npm run check-types` (incl. cross-package shape guard), `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` — clean.
- 1,017 tests pass across the three packages, including: classifier mechanism/edge cases (structural eligibility, gateway gating, exclusion, multi-entity aggregation, order invariance), surface-pinning races (5xx-then-200, chat-before-discovery), all 8 surface×protocol route URLs with per-route auth-scheme assertions, `params.baseUrl` passthrough, Gemini variant wire mappings, and sanitizer round-trips.
- Assistant monorepo `check-types` passes against this branch.

title: Add Bedrock FIPS transport policy for GovCloud
description:
Adds a single per-operation Bedrock transport resolver so chat, model discovery, and Mantle routing consistently honor `AWS_USE_FIPS_ENDPOINT` and the selected AWS profile's `use_fips_endpoint` setting. This provides the partition-aware transport needed for GovCloud while preventing Mantle from sending non-FIPS traffic when FIPS endpoints are required.

## Changes

- Resolve standard or FIPS Bedrock hosts from the standard AWS environment and shared-config sources, with environment values taking precedence and shared-config edits observed by later operations.
- Apply the same transport decision to runtime inference, control-plane model listing, and Mantle discovery; disable and reject Mantle routes under FIPS.
- Add regression coverage for configuration precedence, endpoint selection, routing, model discovery, and existing Bedrock behavior.
- Remove the obsolete duplicate esbuild configuration so the build coordinator remains the single source of build policy.

title: Harden custom provider editing and discovery
description:
Adds the ai-lib support needed for consuming products to edit custom providers safely. It exposes a strict raw user-entry reader, preserves intentional AWS credential clears across legacy migration, and makes custom model discovery reflect the configured endpoint instead of substituting models from hosted providers. It also preserves the public OpenRouter client constructor while allowing custom API base URLs.

## Changes

- **ai-config:** Add a Node-only strict reader for retrieving a custom provider exactly as authored in the user `providers.json` layer, including safe handling for missing, invalid, whitespace-bearing, and prototype-named entries.
- **ai-credentials:** Write tombstones when custom AWS keys are cleared and migrate legacy complete AWS credentials into the keys-only representation during preservation.
- **ai-provider-bridge:** Keep hosted fallback and supplemental model lists limited to built-in providers, make custom endpoint discovery authoritative, and retain OpenRouter constructor compatibility while routing custom base URLs correctly.

## Design decisions

An explicit AWS clear remains on disk as an unauthenticated tombstone so startup migration cannot restore credentials the user removed. Custom provider discovery returns only models reported by that endpoint; users can declare non-discoverable custom models in configuration, while built-in hosted providers retain their curated fallback behavior.

title: Add registrars and credential seams for all custom provider kinds
description:
Extends custom provider support so every supported client kind works as a user-defined `providers.custom.<name>` entry: the config schema accepts `anthropic`/`openai`/`gemini` as custom types, every kind gets a model-discovery registrar in the provider bridge, and custom AWS entries can store keys-only credentials with region/profile resolved from the catalog. This is the ai-lib half of the assistant monorepo's custom provider management UI (consumed via a gitlink bump there).

## Changes

- **ai-config**: custom `type` union extended with `anthropic`, `openai`, `gemini` (base-only variants; required-key kinds), `providers.schema.json` regenerated, and a canonical OpenRouter base-URL normalizer (accepts host-only or `/api/v1` forms, returns the API base) exported from the pure entry so forms, fetchers, and clients share it.
- **ai-credentials**: the three new kinds added to `SUPPORTED_CUSTOM_CLIENT_KIND_VALUES` and `CUSTOM_CLIENT_KIND_AUTH_MAP` as apikey (keeps the `TupleEqual` shape guard green), plus a keys-only `awsKeys` record on stored credentials with a host-supplied `awsConnectionForProvider` callback in `createStoreBackend` — `normalize()` combines stored keys with catalog connection data into a complete `aws-credentials` source, so no caller ever sees keys-only material. `awsKeys` and legacy `awsAuth` are mutually exclusive (legacy wins if both somehow present); the runtime Zod schema is extended accordingly.
- **ai-provider-bridge**: custom registrars for every kind lacking one (`anthropic`, `openai`, `gemini`, `deepseek`, `openrouter`, `ms-foundry`, `ollama`, `lmstudio`, `aws`, `google-vertex`, `snowflake`), each registering both the custom-ID model fetcher and the kind-keyed client factory. Each provider module is refactored around one provider-ID-parameterized fetcher builder shared by the built-in and custom registrars so they cannot drift. `OpenRouterClient` now takes the normalized base URL, so custom OpenRouter endpoints receive chat requests (previously hardcoded to `openrouter.ai`).

## Design decisions

- Custom `anthropic`/`openai`/`gemini` entries are required-key kinds: they get no built-in connection defaults and the reused fetchers reject empty keys. Keyless auth-injecting proxies remain served by `openai-compatible`. `positai`/`copilot`/`databricks` stay excluded (product-bound auth flows).
- Keys-only AWS records carry no region: a missing catalog region means unready, never an invented default.

title: Preserve comments in JSONC config mutations
description:
Previously, whenever Posit Assistant updated `providers.json`, it converted the settings back to plain JSON and replaced the entire file. The settings remained correct, but user-added comments and hand formatting were lost.

This change updates only the values that changed, preserving the rest of the file while keeping the same validation and write-safety guarantees.

## Changes

- Adds a browser-safe `ai-config/jsonc` entry with round-trip JSON serialization normalization, sequential structural edits, source-format inference, duplicate-key ambiguity rejection, and semantic postcondition checks.
- Preserves comments around unchanged siblings during additions and deletions, including object headers, trailing comments, trailing commas, CRLF line endings, and unusual indentation.
- Skips disk writes for value-identical mutations while detecting in-place mutations that return the same object reference.

## Verification

Regression coverage includes comments, structural additions and deletions, arrays, duplicates, no-op and in-place mutations, CRLF and indentation inference, and `JSON.stringify` serialization edge cases.

## Breaking changes

Value-identical `mutateProvidersConfig` callbacks no longer rewrite the file. Callers that relied on a no-op mutation to update timestamps or trigger watchers must perform a real value change.

title: Sanitize tool-call IDs on the Anthropic Messages wire
description:
## Problem

The Anthropic Messages API validates `tool_use.id` / `tool_result.tool_use_id` against `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`. Other wires accept arbitrary IDs — e.g. Kimi K3 emits `<toolName>:<counter>` like `ls:0`, with the counter resetting per turn so duplicates across history are the norm. When a conversation containing such IDs is replayed to an Anthropic-wire model (model switch mid-conversation, `/compact` summarizing with Claude Haiku), the API rejects the request:

```
Error making request (HTTP 400): messages.1.content.1.tool_use.id: String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$'
```

Fixes posit-dev/assistant#2016.

## Fix

The constraint is a property of the **target wire**, so Anthropic-wire clients now sanitize outbound IDs unconditionally via a new `sanitizeToolCallIdsForAnthropic` helper (`tool-call-ids.ts`):

- **Base**: deterministic character replacement (`[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]` → `-`); empty IDs fall back to `call`.
- **Uniqueness**: rewritten ID = `<base>-<i>` where `i` is the message index in the outbound array. Pairing is positional: a `tool-result` in a `tool` message at `j` uses `j-1`; a provider-executed result in an assistant message uses its own index. Deterministic and prompt-cache-stable because history is append-only.
- **Conforming duplicates** (same ID used by a call in an earlier message) are index-suffixed via first-occurrence tracking on tool-*calls* — results mirror their paired call. (A naive seen-set over all parts would break pairing, since results legitimately repeat their call's ID.)
- **No-op fast path**: conforming first-use IDs pass through untouched; pure-Claude histories get the input array back by reference.
- **Observability**: warns on non-conforming IDs, same-message base collisions, and orphan `tool-result` parts.

Wiring goes through a shared `streamTextAnthropicWire()` choke point so future Anthropic-wire clients get sanitization by default: AnthropicClient, PositAiClient (`anthropic-messages` branch), and SnowflakeClient (`chatAnthropic`) use the wrapper; BedrockClient and GoogleVertexClient sanitize conditionally on their Anthropic routes since those `streamText` call sites are shared across protocols.

## Tests

- 11 sanitizer unit tests: deterministic rewrite, positional pairing (both result kinds), cross-turn duplicates (`ls:0` in two turns), same-turn parallel calls, conforming-duplicate suffixing, empty-ID fallback, no-op passthrough, collision/orphan warnings.
- Wire-level regression test through `PositAiClient` with the observed Kimi `ls:0` format repeated across two turns, asserting the serialized request body contains only pattern-conforming, unique, paired IDs. Verified to fail on the unfixed code.

Full bridge suite (286 tests) and monorepo `check-types` pass.

title: Add multi-protocol Portkey gateway provider
description:
Adds a first-class `portkey` provider so organizations routing LLM traffic through a [Portkey](https://portkey.ai/) gateway can use it with each model speaking its natural wire protocol, mirroring the landed LiteLLM provider. Two deployment shapes are supported: hosted Portkey (`https://api.portkey.ai/v1`, Portkey API key, Model Catalog `@provider/model` ids with automatic discovery) and a self-hosted OSS gateway (the stored key is one upstream's key, models are user-declared). Claude models route over the Anthropic-shaped `/v1/messages` passthrough so explicit prompt-cache breakpoints and thinking signatures survive; other families route over the OpenAI-shaped endpoints. The provider is conservative where verification is still pending: hosted discovery currently stamps Claude-family models only, because hosted Portkey behavior could not be probed without an account.

Portkey can also back `providers.custom.<name>` entries with `type: "portkey"`. The custom provider id owns model-fetch/cache identity and model stamping, while chat resolves through the factory registered under the `portkey` client kind, so live type changes follow the current catalog entry. Current user surfaces support a keyless, noncanonical self-hosted gateway or credential-injecting front proxy: models use bare upstream ids declared in `models.custom`, and the ordinary self-hosted path performs no HTTP discovery. A securely stored key for a custom id can reach the shared hosted fetcher, but the canonical hosted origin always requires a non-empty key and there is no custom-id credential UI or environment mapping yet.

## Changes

- **ai-config**: `portkey` added to the provider/client-kind vocabulary, built-in schema/catalog builder, and the base-only `providers.custom` discriminated union (with `providers.schema.json` regenerated); `stripCatalogSlug` exported as the single owner of the `@slug/` id convention; `model-capabilities/portkey-helpers.ts` with `classifyPortkeyModel` (one per-entry decision object — family, capability model id, supported/excluded with reason, protocol — consumed by both discovery filtering and capability stamping) and `getPortkeyModelCapabilities` (Anthropic/OpenAI helper delegation, conservative fallback); canonical hosted base-URL constant in the base-URL policy module; `PORTKEY_BASE_URL` connection env mapping.
- **ai-provider-bridge**: new `providers/portkey-provider.ts` built around a single `resolvePortkeyConnection` seam that both the client factory and model fetchers consume — required base URL, hosted-vs-OSS classification (exact canonical HTTPS origin only; lookalike hosts classify as OSS, `http://api.portkey.ai` is a local error before any request), mode-dependent key validation (hosted requires a non-empty key; OSS permits an empty key for an injecting proxy), `/v1` normalization, and case-insensitive provider-local filtering of `x-portkey-api-key`/`x-portkey-virtual-key` from `customHeaders`. The chat client is a protocol-dispatching wrapper over one `AnthropicClient` and one `OpenAIClient` delegate (mirroring the LiteLLM dispatcher), with a same-gateway check that rejects per-request `baseUrl` overrides pointing at a different host before any request is made. Model discovery uses the `fetchFresh` seam on `createCachedModelFetcher` so Portkey owns its hosted pagination loop (with an atomic no-progress guard), the OSS no-fetch short-circuit, and the chat-vs-discovery header split (routing headers never sent to `GET /v1/models`). `registerCustomPortkeyProvider` registers a custom-id fetcher with independent cache/model identity and the shared kind-keyed client factory. Also fixes blank AI-SDK error messages (`clarifyBlankRequestError` in `ai-sdk-helpers.ts`) surfaced by Portkey's error shapes, benefiting all AI-SDK clients.
- **ai-credentials**: `PORTKEY_API_KEY` env mapping for the built-in provider, plus the custom `portkey` auth descriptor (`apikey`, optional at catalog-synthesis time so a base-URL-only OSS/front-proxy connection can run).

## Design decisions

- **Base URL is required, not defaulted.** For Portkey the URL determines what the stored key *is* (a Portkey key vs. an upstream provider's key), so defaulting it would silently reinterpret the secret — a self-hoster's forgotten URL would send their upstream key to hosted Portkey. Key-only configs instead fail locally, before any network request, with an error naming `PORTKEY_BASE_URL` and the configure form.
- **Connection resolution owns mode validity.** Custom catalog synthesis may produce an empty API key when a base URL is present, but `resolvePortkeyConnection` decides whether that credential is valid for the resolved deployment mode: hosted rejects empty/whitespace keys locally, while OSS accepts an empty key for a credential-injecting proxy. Discovery and chat consume the same rule.
- **Custom fetchers are id-keyed and the client factory is kind-keyed.** Each custom gateway gets independent cache state and correctly stamped model ids. Chat follows the catalog's current `clientKind`, avoiding a stale custom-id factory after a live `providers.json` type change.
- **Secret headers are filtered provider-locally**, never in the shared SDK-managed header filter: those names are Portkey credentials, and a global rule would strip them from existing non-Portkey gateway configurations. The stored key is re-added as a provider-owned header after sanitization so config can never override it.
- **Hosted discovery stamps Claude-family only** until the hosted probe gate can run (no Portkey account was available); other families are excluded with a recorded reason rather than shipped unverified. Widening is additive when the probes run.
- **The dispatcher is mirrored from LiteLLM, not extracted**: Portkey's per-mode credential wiring (hosted needs `x-portkey-api-key` on both delegates) does not parameterize cleanly; the convention stays documented in `providerGuide.md`.

## Verification

Probed against a local OSS gateway (1.15.2): streaming `/v1/messages` passthrough, `/v1/chat/completions` with tools across OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini upstreams, stateless encrypted-reasoning continuity over `/v1/responses`, and Bedrock passthrough with cache and thinking intact. Custom-provider tests cover schema/catalog preservation, custom-id model stamping and Portkey capability inference, operation without the built-in registrar, keyless OSS no-fetch behavior, and local rejection of keyless hosted discovery/chat. ai-lib check-types (including the shape guards), lint, and all package test suites pass.

## Not included

- Hosted Portkey verification (blocked on account access; the provider ships conservative until then).
- A user-facing credential form or environment mapping for arbitrary custom provider ids. Custom Portkey is therefore documented as keyless/noncanonical on current user surfaces; use the built-in provider for one keyed gateway.
- Multi-upstream OSS connections (needs a multi-secret credential shape).

## Known limitations

- OSS gateway 1.15.2 is unusable from a Node client without a shim: every streaming request 500s under Node 24 (gateway bug in undici header handling), and under Bun it mislabels `Content-Encoding: gzip`. A fixed gateway release resolves both upstream.

title: Add litellm provider (built-in and custom client kind)
description:
Adds a `litellm` provider so LiteLLM gateways work with full Anthropic-protocol features (explicit prompt-cache breakpoints, thinking-block preservation) instead of the degraded openai-compatible path. The provider targets LiteLLM's unified `/v1/messages` endpoint by reusing `AnthropicClient` with a normalized base URL, and discovers models from `/v1/model/info`. Consumed by posit-dev/assistant#1876's implementation PR.

## Changes

- **ai-provider-bridge**: `litellm` provider ID and registrar (`registerLitellmProvider`); client factory wrapping `AnthropicClient` that normalizes both the constructor base URL and the per-request `params.baseUrl` routing override through `litellmV1BaseUrl()` (the raw override previously won and chat 404'd); cached `/v1/model/info` fetcher tolerant of null-metadata entries (Ollama-backed aliases) with empty fallback models; a second registrar `registerCustomLitellmProvider(registry, providerId, logger)` for custom gateway entries — per-id model fetchers with the custom id stamped into discovered models and independent caches, while the client factory is registered idempotently under the kind key `"litellm"` so chat resolution goes through the `clientKind` fallback and cannot go stale when an entry's type changes on live catalog reload.

title: Allow comments in `providers.json`, and make robust to unknown fields
description:
# Allow comments in `providers.json`, and make robust to unknown fields

Before this change, `providers.json` was handled pretty strictly: if there were any comments, or any fields that weren't specified in schema, then the code would return an empty `{}` object to represent the configuration.

This PR allows `providers.json` reads to preserve valid provider settings when the file contains JSONC syntax or an unknown or invalid provider block. Reads now return structured, sourced issue snapshots for anything they skip, while mutations remain strict so a programmatic rewrite can never silently delete configuration it does not understand.

## Changes

- Parse user-authored provider configuration as JSONC and preserve unsafe object keys through validation.
- Salvage valid root, built-in provider, and custom provider entries at whole-block granularity with explicit diagnostics for every discarded value.
- Add report-first resolve, load, and watch APIs while retaining the existing catalog-only compatibility APIs and logging behavior.
- Emit complete, structurally deduplicated issue snapshots for file, environment, legacy Positron, resolver, and watcher paths.
- Keep mutations strict and byte-preserving when the current file contains invalid or unknown configuration.
- Report JSONC syntax errors as 1-based line/column (handling LF, CRLF, and CR line endings) instead of raw character offsets, on both the read and mutation paths.
- Classify every whole-source failure — an unparseable or unreadable file, a whole-file salvage degrade (non-object root/`providers`, unsupported `version`), an invalid env fragment, or malformed legacy enforced settings — as an error-severity issue with an empty path, while per-key salvage drops remain warnings scoped to the dropped key. Hosts can therefore surface only whole-source failures in the UI and keep validation drops log-only.

Discover invokable Amazon Bedrock model IDs with `ListInferenceProfiles` instead of deriving them from region-name prefixes. This lets consumers list correct models in Canada, the Middle East, Africa, South America, and future AWS regions while preserving the legacy fallback when profile discovery is unavailable.

The PR also moves Bedrock's `us-east-1` default out of resolved provider connections so stored user regions retain precedence.

## Changes

- Discover and paginate active system-defined inference profiles, select IDs deterministically, and contain permission or service failures within discovery.
- Join inference profiles to foundation models, treating successful discovery as authoritative and using prefix construction only as a fallback in legacy region families.
- Apply the built-in `us-east-1` default at credential synthesis instead of catalog resolution.
- Add regression coverage for default precedence, fallback behavior, pagination, error handling, and profile selection.

A successful profile listing is the source of truth for the calling region; missing models are skipped rather than assigned guessed IDs. When discovery is denied or fails, existing `us`/`eu`/`apac`/`us-gov` regions retain prefix-based behavior, while other region families return no guessed Converse models.

title: Split the legacy-positron-enforced layer behind an independent loader option
description:
Companion PRs (land after this one): assistant posit-dev/assistant#1996, positron posit-dev/positron#15375 (supersedes #15371). Both pin their submodule at this branch's tip — bump the pins to the merged sha if this squashes.

## Problem

The `legacyPositronSettings` loader option enables **both** legacy layers at once: `legacy-positron` (user-set legacy settings, below `user`) and `legacy-positron-enforced` (`POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS`, above `user`). Positron ≥ 2026.08 migrates the legacy provider settings — `authentication.*` connection/credential settings, provider enablement toggles, and model overrides — into providers.json (posit-dev/positron#15121) **without clearing them** (old builds and settings sync still read the legacy channel), so on migrated hosts the reader layer resurrects stale values: clear a migrated providers.json setting and the old settings.json value silently comes back. Users have to clear both places. But the enforced admin channel must keep working there — and dropping the reader today drops both.

## What this does

Each layer becomes an independent opt-in on `LoadCatalogOptions` (and therefore `WatchCatalogOptions`):

| Option | Controls |
| --- | --- |
| `legacyPositronSettings` (existing reader) | **Only** the `legacy-positron` layer now |
| `legacyPositronEnforcedSettings` (new `boolean`) | The `legacy-positron-enforced` layer: unset/false → off, `true` → on |

- `createLegacyPositronSourceProviders` (loader-internal, `sources.ts`) takes `{ reader?, enforcedSettings }` and stays the single assembly point, so the load and watch paths can't diverge on which options enable which layers.
- Rank order unchanged: `enforced > legacy-positron-enforced > env > user > legacy-positron > default`.
- **Semantic break, deliberate:** a reader alone no longer enables the enforced layer. Safe because ai-lib is consumed only via submodule pins updated in lockstep; standalone consumers (Notebooks) pass neither option.

Who passes what after the companion PRs: Positron core catalogs (always ≥ 2026.08) pass only the flag; the assistant extension passes the flag on any Positron plus the reader only on pre-migration Positron (< 2026.08); every other host passes neither.

## Testing

- `npm run build`, `check-types` (incl. shape guard), `lint`, `format:check` all clean.
- `npm test`: ai-config **284** passed (new pins: reader alone does **not** enable the enforced layer; flag alone folds the enforced layer into the load path without a reader; flag folds it into watch-path rebuilds), ai-credentials **134** passed.
- ai-provider-bridge has 6 pre-existing failures on `main` (1c47e7e) in `openai-explicit-prompt-caching-wire.test.ts` — reproduced on a clean checkout, unrelated to this change.
- Validated live through the companion branches in a dev Positron (2026.08): with only `legacyPositronEnforcedSettings: true`, clearing a migrated providers.json value no longer falls back to the stale legacy setting, and `POSITRON_ENFORCED_SETTINGS` still applies above the user file.
